title: Female Life Stages for Cardiovascular Disease Prevention and Management in Girls and Women: A Case-Based Approach.
abstract: Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of death among women in the United States and worldwide, yet current approaches to prevention and management do not fully account for female-specific biology. To address this need, the American Heart Association, in collaboration with the American Academy of Pediatrics, the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and the Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine, published a Presidential Advisory defining the Female Life Stage construct, which defines four distinct stages across the life course: Perimenarche (Stage 1), Ovarian Cycling (Stage 2), Perimenopause (Stage 3), and Postmenopause (Stage 4), with pregnancy including the time before and after (Peripregnancy period) recognized as a distinct life period when cardiovascular risk may be modified.1 To provide examples of how this framework and the accompanying consensus guidance published in an accompanying Scientific Statement can be translated into a personalized care approach, this special report presents six hypothetical cases spanning the Female Life Stages, including adolescence and young adulthood, the peripartum period, midlife, perimenopause, and postmenopause.2 These cases illustrate how a female-specific life course framework that reflects hormonally-mediated physiologic transitions can promote earlier recognition of cardiovascular risk, guide cardiovascular screening and inform cardiovascular management. The cases underscore how hormonal health (e.g., menstrual cycle assessment, pregnancy planning and prevention, assessing and managing perimenopausal and postmenopausal symptoms) and psychosocial health (e.g., anxiety, depression, disordered eating) have cardiovascular implications. Moreover, this approach integrates well-established female-specific cardiovascular risk factors (e.g., premature menopause and adverse pregnancy outcomes), in addition to less well-recognized risk factors (e.g., early menarche, polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome). We also review key evidence to inform a patient-centered approach to exogenous hormone therapy and associated cardiovascular risks for a variety of indications, including management of abnormal uterine bleeding, ovarian suppression, pregnancy prevention, and menopausal symptoms. By contextualizing the Female Life Stage framework within practical case scenarios, this article provides clinicians with a structured, evidence-based approach to improve cardiovascular prevention and management for girls and women.

score.why_it_matters: It translates multi-society guidance on female-specific biology into actionable clinical case scenarios spanning perimenarche through postmenopause.
score.bottom_line: Cardiovascular risk assessment in women should systematically integrate hormonal milestones and reproductive history, including adverse pregnancy outcomes, polycystic ovarian syndrome, and menopause timing, into longitudinal preventive care.

title: Comprehensive Centers of Excellence for Women's Cardiovascular Care: A Science Advisory From the American Heart Association, American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine.
abstract: Improving cardiovascular health in women is an urgent public health priority given the persistent and pervasive gaps in awareness, prevention, and management of cardiovascular disease in this population. Advances in scientific understanding have led to increased recognition of female-specific considerations in cardiovascular disease, which informed the development of the Female Life Stage construct by the American Heart Association in collaboration with the American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine. This construct integrates assessment of hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health across life stages. However, gaps remain in operationalizing this construct and optimizing the delivery of patient-centered, interdisciplinary care among women. Over the past several decades, women's cardiovascular centers have emerged as leaders, expanded rapidly, and elevated the recognition of cardiovascular diseases that exclusively, disproportionately, or differently affect women (eg, myocardial infarction with nonobstructive coronary arteries, spontaneous coronary artery dissection, Takotsubo syndrome). In this science advisory, we describe the current landscape of women's cardiovascular centers and propose a national infrastructure to support the expansion of dedicated Comprehensive Centers of Excellence for Women's Cardiovascular Care. These centers are conceptualized as interdisciplinary care models comprising 4 defining pillars: interdisciplinary clinical care, education and training, research, and community engagement. By establishing integrated pathways that span clinical disciplines, these centers can reduce fragmentation, enhance earlier risk identification, and expand opportunities to increase representation of women in clinical research. In doing so, they offer a bold opportunity for a scalable and equitable model to improve cardiovascular health for all women.

title: A Female-Specific Life Course Approach to the Prevention and Management of Cardiovascular Disease: A Presidential Advisory From the American Heart Association, American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine.
abstract: Cardiovascular disease is the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in women, contributes markedly to healthcare expenditures, and is projected to increase substantially by 2050 if current trends continue. There is growing recognition of the complex role of sex as a biologic variable and its influence on cardiovascular health and disease. However, cardiovascular risk remains underrecognized and underaddressed in girls and women, particularly as it relates to female-specific exposure to sex hormones (both endogenous and exogenous), which are systemic modulators of cardiovascular biology. Moreover, girls and women uniquely experience fragmented care spanning specialties, including pediatrics, adolescent medicine, primary care, obstetrics and gynecology, maternal-fetal medicine, cardiology, endocrinology, hematology, and neurology. Consequently, there is a need for a unified life course approach that addresses the female-specific interconnectedness of hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health. To address these gaps, the American Heart Association, in collaboration with the American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine, established a Female Life Stage framework to optimize the prevention and management of cardiovascular disease in girls and women. Physiologic changes in sex hormones define clinically distinct life stages (ie, perimenarche, ovarian cycling, perimenopause, postmenopause), which directly inform female-specific considerations for screening, prevention, and management of cardiovascular disease. This presidential advisory details the framework and its scientific rationale, highlights opportunities for implementation across settings, and identifies priorities for research, clinician education, patient advocacy, and policy. This framework offers a transformative opportunity to equitably improve cardiovascular health for all girls and women.

title: Consensus Guidance for the Female-Specific Prevention and Management of Cardiovascular Disease: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association, American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine.
abstract: There is growing recognition that the optimal prevention and management of cardiovascular disease in girls and women requires attention to sex-specific considerations relevant to the interconnected domains of hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health across the life course. Dysregulation in these health domains tends to co-occur and is associated with increased risk of cardiovascular disease. However, healthcare for girls and women is uniquely fragmented across clinical specialties, including pediatrics, adolescent medicine, primary care, obstetrics, maternal-fetal medicine, gynecology, cardiology, endocrinology, hematology, and neurology. Furthermore, inconsistent alignment across society guidelines contributes to missed opportunities to optimize cardiovascular health. Therefore, the American Heart Association, American Academy of Pediatrics, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists, and Society for Maternal-Fetal Medicine convened a multisociety science advisory group and developed the Female Life Stage construct. This construct defines 4 distinct and clinically meaningful stages-perimenarche (S1), ovarian cycling (S2), perimenopause (S3), and postmenopause (S4)-to enable female-specific screening, prevention, and treatment considerations. In addition, this construct incorporates pregnancy as a unique modifying life event when cardiovascular risk may emerge or be unmasked (eg, adverse pregnancy outcomes). This scientific statement crosswalks major society guidelines, synthesizes the evidence, and provides consensus-based clinical guidance for each Female Life Stage and interconnected health domain (ie, hormonal, psychosocial, and cardiovascular health). We conclude with a call to action to improve clinical workflows, enhance clinician education, and address scientific and implementation gaps to improve cardiovascular health in girls and women.

score.why_it_matters: This multisociety consensus bridges cardiology, pediatrics, and obstetrics/gynecology to establish a harmonized, life-stage framework for female-specific cardiovascular risk stratification and prevention.
score.bottom_line: Cardiovascular risk assessment in females should be tailored across four key life stages—perimenarche, ovarian cycling, perimenopause, and postmenopause—with pregnancy and adverse pregnancy outcomes recognized as critical windows of unmasked risk. Clinicians should systematically integrate reproductive and hormonal milestones into routine cardiovascular prevention and management workflows.

title: Cardiovascular resilience in centenarians.
abstract: Centenarians - individuals aged ≥100 years - provide a unique human model for understanding resilience to cardiovascular ageing. Although cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, including hypertension, heart failure, atrial fibrillation and chronic kidney disease, are common in centenarians, their onset is typically delayed relative to that in individuals aged 80-100 years. Centenarians characteristically have structural changes in the heart and vessels, including concentric left ventricular remodelling, increased myocardial stiffness and vascular ageing, but often without the expected burden of myocardial infarction or overt heart failure. Their cardiometabolic profile is generally favourable, marked by preserved insulin sensitivity in cohorts with a low prevalence of diabetes mellitus, mid-range lipid levels and a low prevalence of obesity. Centenarians also have a distinctive inflammatory and gastrointestinal phenotype, characterized by chronic low-grade inflammation with elevated anti-inflammatory signalling, a gut microbiome that more closely resembles that of younger adults, and preserved intestinal barrier integrity. Genetically and epigenetically, exceptional longevity reflects highly polygenic contributions, selective maintenance of genomic stability and markedly younger epigenetic age compared with chronological age. In this Review, we summarize data on the cardiovascular system among centenarians by framing observations of longevity as a composite of delayed pathology, adaptive compensation and survivorship selection. Understanding the biological, behavioural and environmental mechanisms underlying cardiovascular resilience in extreme longevity might inform strategies to extend cardiovascular healthspan across all ages.

score.why_it_matters: Understanding the biology of extreme longevity provides mechanistic insights into delayed cardiovascular pathology, vascular aging, and natural cardioprotection.
score.bottom_line: Centenarians exhibit significant subclinical structural cardiovascular aging without the expected clinical burden of heart failure or infarction, driven by preserved metabolic health, genomic stability, and favorable inflammatory balance. This narrative review highlights potential targets to enhance population-level cardiovascular healthspan.

title: A Novel Method for Assessing Left Bundle Branch Capture Using the Bidirectional Conduction Time Difference Between Left Bundle Branch Area Pacing and Coronary Sinus Leads.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) is an established conduction system pacing strategy; however, confirming left bundle branch (LBB) capture remains challenging.
OBJECTIVE: We propose a novel method for LBB capture confirmation based on the bidirectional conduction time difference between the LBBAP and coronary sinus (CS) leads.
METHODS: This observational study included 60 patients undergoing de novo left bundle branch-optimized cardiac resynchronization therapy. LBB capture was defined by (1) paced QRS transition, (2) LBB potential with current of injury, or (3) ΔV6 R-wave peak time ≥10 ms. LBBAP-to-CS and CS-to-LBBAP conduction times were measured. ΔLBB-CS ([CS-to-LBBAP] - [LBBAP-to-CS]) was compared between nonselective LBB pacing (NS-LBBP) and left ventricular septal pacing (LVSP).
RESULTS: Among 60 patients (74.7±10.4 years; 42 men), 25 had left bundle branch block and 17 had non-specific intraventricular conduction delay. LBB capture was confirmed in 45 patients (75.0%). LBBAP-to-CS was 114.3±28.0 ms during NS-LBBP (n=43) and 134.2±19.0 ms during LVSP (n=29), whereas CS-to-LBBAP was 143.4±28.5 ms (n=60). ΔLBB-CS was greater during NS-LBBP than LVSP (27.5±9.9 vs. 7.9±7.4 ms, P<0.01). Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis identified a 21.5 ms cutoff for LBB capture (74.4% sensitivity; 100% specificity; area under curve [AUC] 0.95). In patients with baseline LBBB (n=25), a 20.5 ms cutoff for LBB capture yielded 92.9% sensitivity, 100% specificity, and an AUC of 0.99.
CONCLUSION: ΔLBB-CS ≥ 21.5ms may serve as a novel adjunctive marker of LBB capture during LOT-CRT, with greater diagnostic accuracy at a 20.5 ms cutoff in patients with baseline LBBB.

score.why_it_matters: Differentiating true left bundle branch capture from myocardial septal pacing remains a technical challenge during conduction system pacing, and this study offers a novel physiological metric when a coronary sinus lead is co-implanted.
score.bottom_line: In patients undergoing LOT-CRT, a bidirectional conduction time difference between the LBBAP and CS leads (ΔLBB-CS) ≥21.5 ms demonstrated high specificity for confirming left bundle branch capture.

title: Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitor Use and Levels of Hemoglobin, Markers of Iron Metabolism, and Erythropoiesis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Clinical Trials.
abstract:
IMPORTANCE: In randomized clinical trials, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor use was associated with increased hemoglobin and hematocrit compared with placebo. However, the magnitude and importance of this association remain unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the associations between SGLT2 inhibitor use and levels of hemoglobin, hematocrit, and markers of iron metabolism and erythropoiesis compared with placebo or active comparator.
DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) were searched from inception to July 22, 2026.
STUDY SELECTION: Randomized, double-masked clinical trials comparing SGLT2 inhibitor use with placebo or active comparators in patients with 1 or more of the following conditions: cardiovascular disease, diabetes, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease.
DATA EXTRACTION AND SYNTHESIS: Three reviewers independently extracted data and results were pooled using random-effects meta-analysis.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Primary outcomes were changes in hemoglobin and hematocrit. Secondary outcomes were changes in red blood cell concentration, erythropoietin (EPO), and iron measures (serum iron, ferritin, transferrin saturation, and hepcidin).
RESULTS: A total of 85 randomized clinical trials were analyzed (median [IQR] duration, 24 [12-32] weeks), including 70 543 participants (mean [SD] age, 62.4 [9.4] years; 25 334 female [35.9%]). Mean (SD) baseline hemoglobin was 13.6 (1.5) g/dL; baseline hematocrit was 41.5% (4.9). Seventy-eight clinical trials (67 208 participants) compared SGLT2 inhibitors with placebo, and 7 clinical trials (3335 participants) used active comparators, most commonly sitagliptin (2 trials [1158 participants]). From baseline to follow-up, hemoglobin changed by 0.55 g/dL (95% CI, 0.49 to 0.61 g/dL; P < .001) in the SGLT2 inhibitor group, and -0.08 g/dL (95% CI, -0.13 to -0.03 g/dL; P = .003) in the control group (difference, 0.60 g/dL; 95% CI, 0.55 to 0.66 g/dL; P < .001). From baseline to follow-up, hematocrit changed by 2.17% (95% CI, 1.95% to 2.39%; P < .001) in the SGLT2 inhibitor group and -0.13% (95% CI, -0.28% to 0.01%; P = .07) in the control group (difference, 2.36%; 95% CI, 2.19% to 2.52%; P < .001). Of the 6 secondary outcomes, 4 showed significant associations with SGLT2 inhibitors, including increased EPO (2.35 mIU/mL in SGLT2 inhibitor group vs 0.04 mIU/mL in control group; difference, 2.11 mIU/mL [95% CI, 0.5-3.71 mIU/mL]; P = .01) and decreased transferrin saturation (-2.2% in SGLT2 inhibitor group vs -0.10% in control group; difference, -0.84% [95% CI, -1.21% to -0.47%]; P < .001).
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In a meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials, compared with control, SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with small statistically significant increases in hemoglobin and hematocrit levels. The clinical significance of these findings is unclear.

score.why_it_matters: This comprehensive meta-analysis of over 70,000 trial participants confirms that SGLT2 inhibitors induce a modest rise in hemoglobin and hematocrit via erythropoietin stimulation and iron utilization.
score.bottom_line: SGLT2 inhibitors consistently produce modest increases in hemoglobin (~0.6 g/dL) and hematocrit (~2.4%) driven by erythropoietin release; clinicians should recognize this as an expected drug effect rather than a reason for diagnostic workup of secondary polycythemia.

title: Immediate Complete Revascularization During Index Admission in Older Patients With ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether age affects the comparative treatment effect of immediate complete revascularization (CR) vs staged CR during the index admission in patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction and multivessel disease remains unknown.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to assess how age influences clinical outcomes in patients with with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction and multivessel disease randomized to immediate or in-hospital staged CR.
METHODS: This is a secondary analysis of the OPTION-STEMI (Optimal Timing of Fractional Flow Reserve-Guided Complete Revascularization for Non-Infarct-Related Artery in ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction with Multivessel Disease) trial, which included 994 patients randomized to immediate or in-hospital staged CR. The primary endpoint at 1 year, defined as a composite of all-cause death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or any unplanned revascularization, was analyzed according to age and CR strategy.
RESULTS: A significant interaction was found between age, as a continuous variable, and CR strategy for the primary endpoint (interaction P = 0.015). The HR for the primary endpoint was initially higher in the staged CR arm until approximately 67 years, after which it increased steadily in the immediate CR arm. In the binary analysis, a significantly higher incidence of the primary endpoint was observed in the immediate CR arm compared with the staged CR arm in patients ≥70 years (45 of 202 [22.3%] vs 29 of 210 [13.8%]; HR: 1.68; 95% CI: 1.06-2.69; log-rank P = 0.029), but not in patients <70 years (20 of 296 [6.8%] vs 24 of 286 [8.4%]; HR: 0.80; 95% CI: 0.45-1.45; log-rank P = 0.470) (multiplicative interaction P = 0.054; relative excess risk due to interaction P = 0.016).
CONCLUSIONS: This post hoc analysis of the OPTION-STEMI trial demonstrates that older patients experience significantly worse clinical outcomes with immediate CR than with in-hospital staged CR. These findings suggest that age modifies the treatment effect of the CR strategy and warrant confirmation in adequately powered trials (Timing of FFR-guided PCI for Non-IRA in STEMI and MVD [OPTION-STEMI]; NCT04626882).

score.why_it_matters: In older STEMI patients with multivessel disease, immediate complete revascularization during index primary PCI was associated with increased 1-year adverse events compared to in-hospital staged revascularization.
score.bottom_line: A staged approach to non-culprit lesions may be safer than immediate complete revascularization during primary PCI in patients aged 70 and older. While hypothesis-generating, these data advise caution against prolonged single-setting revascularization in elderly STEMI patients.

title: Shared Genetic Architecture Between Mental Disorders and Heart Failure Subtypes: A Comprehensive Multitrait Genome-Wide Analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mental disorders and heart failure frequently co-occur, but their shared genetic architecture remains incompletely understood.
METHODS: Prospective Cox regression analysis in the UK Biobank (UKB) quantified the risk of incident heart failure associated with mental disorders. Linkage disequilibrium score regression estimated genetic correlations, while multitrait genome-wide association and cross-phenotype association analyses identified candidate pleiotropic loci. Statistical fine mapping and gene-level association analyses prioritized candidate variants and genes. Bayesian colocalization assessed evidence for shared candidate variants, and exploratory Gene Ontology biological-process overrepresentation analysis provided descriptive biological context. Single-cell RNA sequencing and genetically informed spatial mapping (gsMap) provided cellular and spatial context for prioritized genes. Geneformer-based in silico perturbation analysis was performed using a cardiac cell atlas of dilated cardiomyopathy to prioritize candidate pleiotropic genes and identify cardiac cell states showing predicted embedding shifts.
RESULTS: Prospective UKB analyses demonstrated that mental disorders, such as posttraumatic stress disorder, depression, and bipolar disorder, were associated with a higher risk of incident heart failure. Multitrait analysis identified 607 pleiotropic variants, with fine-mapping and colocalization converging on prioritized candidate loci, including TMEM18, NKX2-2, and XRN2. Single-cell expression profiling and spatial mapping provided context at the cellular and tissue levels for the prioritized genes. Geneformer-based in silico perturbation prioritized FOXP1 and TMEM106B as leading pleiotropic candidate genes on the basis of their predicted changes in downstream gene embeddings in cardiac cellular contexts.
CONCLUSIONS: This study identifies shared genetic architecture between mental disorders and heart failure and prioritizes candidate pleiotropic genes associated with both. Transcriptomic and in silico perturbation analyses provide exploratory cellular, spatial, and cardiac functional context. Functional validation is required before mechanistic or therapeutic interpretation.

score.why_it_matters: This study highlights pleiotropic genetic loci linking psychiatric disorders to heart failure, providing foundational biological context for their frequent clinical co-occurrence.
score.bottom_line: Mental disorders share significant genetic architecture and pleiotropic loci with incident heart failure. While hypothesis-generating for future translational targets, these genetic findings do not alter current clinical management.

title: Physical Activity and Cardiovascular Risk in Type 2 Diabetes With Normal Body Mass Index and Abdominal Obesity: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic implications of abdominal obesity and moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) in patients with type 2 diabetes who have a normal body mass index remain unclear.
METHODS: This nationwide retrospective cohort study included 323 029 adults with newly diagnosed type 2 diabetes and a normal body mass index (<23 kg/m2) between January 1, 2010, and December 31, 2023, from the Korean National Health Insurance Service database. Abdominal obesity was defined using sex-specific waist circumference thresholds (≥90 cm for men, ≥80 cm for women). MVPA was assessed through standardized self-reported questionnaires administered during routine health screenings. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events, defined as a composite of all-cause death, myocardial infarction, ischemic stroke, or hospitalization for heart failure.
RESULTS: Among the study population, 34 033 (10.5%) had abdominal obesity. During a median follow-up of 6.0 years (interquartile range, 2.6-9.0 years), abdominal obesity was associated with a higher risk of major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (adjusted hazard ratio [HR], 1.13 [95% CI, 1.09-1.17]). Among patients with abdominal obesity, regular MVPA after diagnosis (27.1%) was associated with a significantly lower risk of major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (adjusted HR 0.74 [95% CI, 0.68-0.80]), all-cause mortality (adjusted HR 0.72 [95% CI, 0.65-0.80]), ischemic stroke (adjusted HR 0.77 [95% CI, 0.66-0.89]), and hospitalization for heart failure (adjusted HR 0.75 [95% CI, 0.60-0.93]). The cardiovascular protective effects of MVPA were consistent regardless of statin or antidiabetic medication use.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with type 2 diabetes and a normal body mass index, abdominal obesity was independently associated with a higher risk of major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events. Regular engagement in MVPA showed consistent cardiovascular benefits in this population, irrespective of pharmacotherapy.
REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT07071545.

score.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that central adiposity increases cardiovascular risk even among normal-BMI patients with type 2 diabetes, and that moderate-to-vigorous physical activity substantially mitigates this excess risk.
score.bottom_line: In normal-weight patients with type 2 diabetes, abdominal obesity carries significant cardiovascular excess risk, but regular moderate-to-vigorous exercise is associated with a 26% lower MACCE rate regardless of pharmacotherapy.

title: Not All Strokes Are Equal: Phenotype-Dependent Surgical Timing in Infective Endocarditis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: We evaluated postoperative neurologic and mortality outcomes by stroke-to-surgery timing and stroke phenotype in patients with left-sided infective endocarditis.
METHODS: Adult patients undergoing surgery for infective endocarditis complicated by preoperative stroke between 2004 and 2024 at 2 institutions were stratified by stroke-to-surgery interval (<1 week, 1-4 weeks, 4-6 weeks). The primary outcome was a composite postoperative cerebrovascular event: new stroke, enlarging stroke, or hemorrhagic conversion. Secondary outcomes were operative death and major morbidity events.
RESULTS: Among 2265 patients with left-sided infective endocarditis, 322 met inclusion criteria, of whom 122 (38%) underwent surgery within 1 week, 168 (52%) between 1 and 4 weeks, and 32 (10%) between 4 and 6 weeks. Operative death was similar across groups (P=0.09). Postoperative cerebrovascular events declined with time (<1 week, 21.3%; 1-4 weeks, 11.9%; 4-6 weeks, 9.4%; P=0.015). On multivariable analysis, longer stroke-to-surgery interval was associated with reduced odds of postoperative cerebrovascular events (odds ratio, 0.92/d [95% CI, 0.85-0.98]; P=0.015), driven by early events among patients with intraparenchymal hemorrhage, subarachnoid hemorrhage, and septic emboli. Among ischemic strokes, operative death was lowest with surgery within 1 week (5.8% versus 11.2% at 1-4 weeks; P=0.24). Interval embolization occurred in 10.6% of patients awaiting surgery, most commonly affecting the spleen and kidneys.
CONCLUSIONS: Excess postoperative neurologic risk was concentrated within the first 7 to 10 days and driven by intraparenchymal hemorrhage, subarachnoid hemorrhage, and septic emboli; ischemic stroke showed no appreciable temporal association. Routine delay after ischemic stroke may not be necessary, while a short delay (≈7 days) for hemorrhagic and septic embolic subtypes may be reasonable when hemodynamically feasible.

score.why_it_matters: Provides granular, phenotype-specific evidence on surgical timing in infective endocarditis with neurologic complications, challenging long mandatory delays.
score.bottom_line: Routine surgical delay may be unnecessary following ischemic stroke in infective endocarditis, whereas a shorter delay of 7 to 10 days appears reasonable to mitigate neurological risk in patients with intracranial hemorrhage or septic emboli.

title: Residual Risk From Remnant Cholesterol and Inflammation Despite Lipid-Lowering Therapy and Association With Incident Peripheral Artery Disease in Type 2 Diabetes.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite guideline-recommended lipid-lowering therapy, patients with type 2 diabetes retain a significant residual risk for peripheral artery disease (PAD). The contributions of remnant cholesterol (RC) and systemic inflammation in this treated population, particularly beyond achieved low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, remain incompletely understood.
METHODS: This prospective cohort study included 18 741 participants with type 2 diabetes from the UK Biobank who were free of PAD and were on lipid-lowering therapy at baseline. Plasma RC and hsCRP (high-sensitivity C-reactive protein) levels were measured at baseline. Incident PAD was ascertained over a median follow-up of 13.6 years. Multivariable Cox models were used to estimate hazard ratios after adjustment for demographic, clinical, metabolic, and treatment-related covariates, including low-density lipoprotein cholesterol and baseline coronary artery disease.
RESULTS: During follow-up, incident PAD occurred in 1223 participants (6.5%). Elevated RC and hsCRP levels were each independently linked to an increased risk of PAD. Participants with concurrent elevations in both RC and hsCRP exhibited the highest risk of incident PAD. These associations remained robust across multiple sensitivity analyses, including exclusion of participants with baseline coronary artery disease, removal of events within the initial 2-year follow-up, elimination of individuals with hsCRP >10 mg/L, competing-risk analyses accounting for death, and further adjustment for detailed lipid-lowering therapy categories.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with type 2 diabetes receiving lipid-lowering therapy for primary prevention of PAD, elevated RC and systemic inflammation are independently and jointly associated with future PAD risk. These findings highlight substantial residual risk beyond managed low-density lipoprotein cholesterol and support the need for further strategies targeting both remnant lipoproteins and inflammation in this high-risk population.

score.why_it_matters: Demonstrates that residual atherogenic risk for peripheral artery disease in treated type 2 diabetes is driven in parallel by elevated remnant cholesterol and persistent low-grade inflammation.
score.bottom_line: In patients with type 2 diabetes on lipid-lowering therapy, concurrent elevations in remnant cholesterol and hsCRP identify those at the highest risk for incident PAD, supporting surveillance beyond standard LDL-C control.

title: Sex Differences in the Associations of Age-Related Genetic Predisposition With Incident Atrial Fibrillation: A Prospective Cohort Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Polygenic risks for diseases are age-dependent. However, sex differences in the age-related association between polygenic risk score and incident atrial fibrillation (AF) remain unclear.
METHODS: A prospective cohort study was conducted using UK Biobank data, including 386 154 participants aged 40 to 69 years, with a median follow-up of 15.6 years. High AF polygenic risk score was defined as ≥0.858 (top quintile). Cox regression, 10-fold cross-validated C-statistic, Royston's R2, and population-attributable risk percentages were used to evaluate sex- and age-specific genetic effects on incident AF.
RESULTS: High polygenic risk score was significantly associated with incident AF, and continuous-age analyses showed that the age-related trajectories differed across sexes (P for difference in age-related trajectories=0.005). In age-stratified analyses, the association was numerically higher in men aged 40 to 49 years (hazard ratio [HR], 2.76 versus 2.07 in women; Bonferroni-adjusted P for interaction=0.077), whereas it was higher in women aged 60 to 69 years (HR, 2.22 versus 1.95 in men; Bonferroni-adjusted P for interaction <0.001). Cross-validated prediction analyses showed broadly similar age- and sex-specific patterns. Population-attributable risk of high polygenic risk score gradually declined across age strata in men, whereas it first increased and then decreased in women.
CONCLUSIONS: Age-related genetic predisposition to AF exhibits distinct sex-specific patterns, offering a foundation for personalized risk stratification and prevention strategies tailored to age and sex.

score.why_it_matters: This study demonstrates that the impact of polygenic risk on incident atrial fibrillation varies across age and sex, with genetic burden peaking earlier in men than in women.
score.bottom_line: Polygenic risk scores for atrial fibrillation show age- and sex-dependent effect sizes, but they remain an exploratory epidemiological tool without current indication for routine clinical screening.

title: Outcomes of Intra-Arterial Urokinase After Endovascular Reperfusion for Acute Ischemic Stroke Due to Cardioembolism: A Secondary Analysis of the POST-UK Trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether adjunctive intra-arterial thrombolysis improves outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke due to cardioembolism remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the efficacy and safety of adjunctive intra-arterial urokinase in patients with acute ischemic stroke due to cardioembolism who achieved near-complete to complete reperfusion.
METHODS: This study was a secondary analysis of the POST-UK (Adjunctive Intra-Arterial Urokinase After Near-Complete to Complete Reperfusion for Acute Ischemic Stroke) trial, which was conducted from November 15, 2022, to March 29, 2024. Patients were randomly assigned to the intra-arterial urokinase group or the control group. The primary outcome was disability-free survival at 90 days, defined as a modified Rankin Scale score of 0 to 1. Safety outcomes included 90-day all-cause death, symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage and any intracranial hemorrhage within 48 hours.
RESULTS: Among 209 patients with cardioembolism (median age 73 [interquartile range, 63-81] years; 45.9% men), 106 were assigned to the control group and 103 to the intra-arterial urokinase group. Compared with the control group, adjunctive intra-arterial urokinase significantly increased the odds of disability-free survival at 90 days (adjusted risk ratio, 1.49 [95% CI, 1.08-2.06]; P=0.01; inverse probability of treatment weighting adjusted risk ratio, 1.47 [95% CI, 1.04-2.09]; P=0.03). No significant differences were found between groups in 90-day mortality rate, symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage, or any intracranial hemorrhage within 48 hours.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with acute ischemic stroke due to cardioembolism who achieved near-complete to complete reperfusion, adjunctive intra-arterial urokinase significantly improved disability-free survival at 90 days without increasing the risk of death or intracranial hemorrhage.
REGISTRATION: URL: ChiCTR.org.cn; Unique identifier: ChiCTR2200065617.

score.why_it_matters: Provides randomized secondary evidence that adjunctive intra-arterial thrombolysis after successful thrombectomy for cardioembolic stroke improves disability-free survival without increasing intracranial hemorrhage.
score.bottom_line: In patients with acute ischemic stroke from cardioembolism who achieve successful reperfusion, adjunctive intra-arterial urokinase significantly increased 90-day disability-free survival. While primarily managed by neuro-interventionalists, these findings inform comprehensive post-stroke care for cardiologists managing cardioembolic sources.

title: Thioredoxin-Interacting Protein-Regulated in Development and DNA Damage-Response 1-Driven Macrophage Senescence Promotes Hypoxia-Induced Pulmonary Hypertension.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a life-threatening vascular disorder characterized by pulmonary arterial remodeling and right ventricular failure, posing a significant clinical challenge. Although macrophage dysfunction is implicated in PH pathogenesis, its underlying molecular mechanisms remain elusive.
METHODS: We employed multiomics database analysis, cross-species validation, and functional studies in hypoxia-induced PH models. Myeloid-specific Txnip deletion was achieved via bone marrow transplantation in mice. Mechanistic insights were evaluated through protein-binding assays, cellular senescence analyses in bone marrow-derived macrophages, and co-culture experiments with pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells.
RESULTS: We identified that cellular senescence in pulmonary adventitial macrophages was involved in the pathogenesis of hypoxia-induced PH. Integrated multiomics analysis revealed elevated TXNIP (thioredoxin-interacting protein) expression in perivascular macrophages during hypoxia-induced PH. Myeloid-specific Txnip deletion attenuated hypoxia-induced pulmonary vascular remodeling in mice. Mechanistically, TXNIP binds to and stabilizes the REDD1 (regulated in development and DNA damage-response 1) protein, promoting hypoxia-induced senescence in bone marrow-derived macrophages. Conditioned medium from senescent macrophages subsequently enhanced the proliferation and migration of pulmonary artery smooth muscle cells.
CONCLUSIONS: The TXNIP-REDD1 axis drives hypoxia-induced macrophage senescence, which promotes pulmonary artery smooth muscle cell dysfunction and pulmonary vascular remodeling in hypoxia-induced PH. Targeting the TXNIP-REDD1 pathway may provide a novel therapeutic strategy for hypoxia-induced PH.

score.why_it_matters: Identifies the TXNIP-REDD1 signaling axis in macrophage senescence as a potential molecular contributor to hypoxia-induced pulmonary vascular remodeling.
score.bottom_line: This preclinical rodent study reveals a novel mechanistic pathway in pulmonary hypertension, but findings remain exploratory and do not impact immediate clinical practice.

title: Lipoprotein(a) and Risk Stratification for Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease Across the Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Continuum.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lp(a) (lipoprotein(a)) is an established risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), but its prognostic relevance across the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) continuum remains uncertain. We examined whether Lp(a) was associated with incident ASCVD across CKM stages and whether it provided complementary risk stratification beyond CKM staging.
METHODS: We included 333 321 UK Biobank participants free of clinical cardiovascular disease at baseline and classified them into CKM stages 0 to 3. Elevated Lp(a) was defined as ≥125 nmol/L. The primary outcome was incident ASCVD, defined as coronary artery disease or ischemic stroke. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs), and 10-year absolute risks were estimated using Kaplan-Meier methods.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 15.3 years, 17 581 incident ASCVD events occurred. After adjustment for demographic characteristics, socioeconomic factors, lifestyle factors, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, medications, and CKM stage, elevated Lp(a) was associated with higher ASCVD risk (HR, 1.31 [95% CI, 1.25-1.36]). In joint analyses, risk increased progressively across combined CKM-Lp(a) categories, with the highest risk observed in participants with CKM stage 3 and elevated Lp(a) versus CKM stage 0 and lower Lp(a) (HR, 3.43 [95% CI, 2.74-4.31]). Ten-year ASCVD risk ranged from 0.64% to 16.30%, and the absolute risk difference associated with elevated Lp(a) increased from 0.23% in stage 0 to 2.20% in stage 3.
CONCLUSIONS: Elevated Lp(a) was associated with higher incident ASCVD risk across the CKM continuum. Although relative associations were broadly consistent across CKM stages, absolute risk increments associated with elevated Lp(a) were greater at more advanced CKM stages, supporting the integration of Lp(a) into CKM-based risk stratification for primary prevention.

score.why_it_matters: This study shows that elevated Lipoprotein(a) independently enhances ASCVD risk stratification across the newly defined cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) continuum, yielding the highest absolute risk increments in advanced stages.
score.bottom_line: Elevated Lp(a) (≥125 nmol/L) was independently associated with a 31% higher risk of incident ASCVD across all CKM stages, with 10-year absolute risk differences being tenfold higher in CKM stage 3 compared to stage 0.

title: Role of Plasma Proteins in the Association Between Socioeconomic Status and Cardiovascular Disease Events: Results From Trans-Omics for Precision Medicine Cohorts.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Socioeconomic status (SES) is strongly associated with cardiovascular disease burden and risk. Plasma proteins may elucidate a biological mechanism through which low SES increases the risk of cardiovascular disease.
METHODS: Participants from the following 3 cohorts were included: the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis (n=2139), Jackson Heart Study (n=967), and Women's Health Initiative (n=1104). SES was approximated using a cumulative score (range 0-3) across education, income, and employment status. A meta-analysis of Cox proportional hazards ratios was used to assess the association between SES and incident events for coronary heart disease (CHD) and stroke. Linear regression was used within each cohort to determine associations between SES and Olink proteins (n=1270 proteins) and the results were meta-analyzed across cohorts. Regression-based mediation analysis was used to determine whether the identified proteins were statistical mediators of the association of SES and incident events.
RESULTS: Higher SES scores were associated with a lower risk of CHD (hazard ratio [HR], 0.74 [95% CI, 0.63-0.87]) and stroke (HR, 0.81 [95% CI, 0.66-1.00]). After correcting for multiple testing (P<3.937×10-5), 233 proteins were associated with SES in the meta-analysis. Of these 233 proteins, 21 had a significant indirect effect on SES and CHD. Because the SES-stroke association was not statistically significant, proteins were not tested as mediators.
CONCLUSIONS: Our analysis of multiple cohorts identified evidence of different proteomic pathways associated with SES and cardiovascular disease. This work suggests that exogenous social factors (eg, SES) may influence cardiovascular disease via proteomic profiles.

score.why_it_matters: This study highlights biological pathways, specifically circulating plasma proteins, that partially mediate the established epidemiological link between adverse socioeconomic status and coronary heart disease.
score.bottom_line: While socioeconomic status significantly correlates with distinct proteomic signatures linked to coronary heart disease, these findings remain exploratory and currently do not alter individualized risk stratification or clinical management.

title: Contemporary Burden, Drivers, and Risk-Factor Control Gaps Across Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome Stages in US Adults, 2021 to 2023.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome staging integrates adiposity, metabolic dysfunction, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular disease. Contemporary national estimates of CKM stage distribution, stage drivers, and treatment gaps are needed to inform implementation of the CKM framework.
METHODS: We analyzed adults aged ≥20 years in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 2021 to 2023 fasting subsample. CKM stage was assigned hierarchically using American Heart Association CKM staging criteria. We estimated survey-weighted CKM stage prevalence, national population counts, stage-specific drivers, and risk-factor control and treatment gaps across stages 2 through 4.
RESULTS: The analytic sample included 2958 adults, representing 245.2 million US adults. Overall, 26.4 million adults (10.8%) were stage 0, 56.8 million (23.2%) stage 1, 125.9 million (51.3%) stage 2, 13.4 million (5.5%) stage 3, and 22.7 million (9.3%) stage 4. Stage ≥1 was present in 89.2%, stage ≥2 in 66.1%, and advanced CKM (stages 3-4) in 14.7%. Among stage 1 adults, 85.1% had adiposity and 49.2% had prediabetes. Among adults with stage 2 CKM, hypertension (72.0%), metabolic syndrome (56.1%), and hypertriglyceridemia (41.9%) were common drivers. Among adults with stage 3 CKM, 95.8% met the Predicting Risk of Cardiovascular Disease Events 10-year cardiovascular disease risk criterion. Risk-factor control and treatment gaps were common across stages 2 through 4, including blood pressure ≥130/80 mm Hg in 50.3% to 66.9%, lipid-lowering therapy nonuse among eligible adults in 30.1% to 59.2%, and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol above the target in 64.5% to 73.9%.
CONCLUSIONS: CKM syndrome affects most US adults, with stage-specific drivers and persistent risk-factor control and treatment gaps. These findings provide contemporary benchmarks for CKM surveillance and implementation.

score.why_it_matters: Provides updated national benchmarks demonstrating that nearly 90% of US adults have cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome, with massive undertreatment of blood pressure and dyslipidemia.
score.bottom_line: In this contemporary NHANES analysis, almost 15% of US adults have advanced CKM syndrome (stages 3-4), yet guideline-directed risk-factor control remains poor with high rates of uncontrolled hypertension and lipid-lowering underutilization.

title: Multivariate Trajectories of Cardiometabolic Risk Factors and Complications in Elderly Chinese Patients With Type 2 Diabetes: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The current study aimed to identify the multivariate trajectories of cardiometabolic risk factors in elderly patients with type 2 diabetes and investigate their associations with cardiovascular disease and diabetic kidney disease (DKD).
METHODS: A retrospective cohort of 27 288 patients with type 2 diabetes aged ≥60 years from China's National Basic Public Health Service Program was analyzed. All participants had ≥3 medical examinations from 2018 to 2023. A multivariate latent class mixed model was used to identify the sex-specific multitrajectories of fasting plasma glucose, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and diastolic blood pressure. Binary logistic regression estimated odds ratios (ORs) and 95% CIs for associations with cardiovascular disease, coronary heart disease, stroke, and DKD.
RESULTS: Among elderly male patients, 3 quadratic trajectory groups were identified: stable (87.16%; n=7997), U shape (3.78%; n=347), and inverse U shape (9.06%; n=831). In elderly women, 2 quadratic trajectory groups were identified: stable (87.29%; n=15 810) and inverse U shape (12.71%; n=2303). In men, the U-shape group had elevated risks of cardiovascular disease (OR, 1.66 [95% CI, 1.26-2.20]), coronary heart disease (OR, 1.60 [95% CI, 1.09-2.33]), stroke (OR, 1.58 [95% CI, 1.12-2.23]), and DKD (OR, 1.39 [95% CI, 1.11-1.74]); the inverse U-shape group had increased DKD risk (OR, 1.35 [95% CI, 1.16-1.57]). In women, the inverse U-shape group was associated with coronary heart disease (OR, 1.31 [95% CI, 1.12-1.53]) and DKD (OR, 1.65 [95% CI, 1.51-1.81]).
CONCLUSIONS: Distinct sex-specific trajectories of cardiometabolic risk factors were associated with different risks of cardiovascular and diabetic kidney complications in elderly patients with type 2 diabetes. These findings support early identification and personalized management of adverse trajectories to potentially reduce long-term complications in this population.

score.why_it_matters: Demonstrates that longitudinal, fluctuating trajectories of cardiometabolic risk factors over time correlate with higher cardiovascular and renal risks compared to stable profiles in older adults with type 2 diabetes.
score.bottom_line: Elderly diabetic patients with unstable or fluctuating cardiometabolic risk trajectories (glucose, blood pressure, LDL) face higher risks of cardiovascular disease and diabetic nephropathy. Sustained stability of risk factor control remains an important clinical goal.

title: Testosterone, Testosterone Replacement Therapy, and Cardiovascular Disease: A Contemporary Review.
abstract: Whether low endogenous testosterone is causal for cardiovascular disease, and how the cardiovascular risk of testosterone replacement therapy should now be classified, remain contested, while US labeling has moved in 2 opposing directions within 16 months. We conducted a targeted narrative review reported in accordance with the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles, searching MEDLINE and primary regulatory documents from January 2000 through July 2026. Evidence was graded with a prespecified 3-tier structured author-consensus rating separating established randomized findings, unresolved secondary signals, and evidentiary absence. Low endogenous testosterone is consistently associated with higher all-cause and cardiovascular mortality but most plausibly marks multimorbidity rather than causation. TRAVERSE established that physiologic transdermal testosterone replacement therapy was noninferior to placebo for 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events over ∼3 years, within a permissive margin and against a 61% discontinuation rate. Observational analyses linking normalization to lower mortality were not reproduced under randomization. Atrial fibrillation, pulmonary embolism, acute kidney injury, fracture, and noncalcified plaque progression remain unresolved. Blood pressure rises across the class; on ambulatory monitoring the magnitude differs by individual product rather than by route. Long-term exposure and nontransdermal formulations remain untested, and the age-related-hypogonadism limitation of use is now proposed for removal. Noninferiority over 3 years should not be read as long-term clinical equivalence. Safe use of testosterone replacement therapy requires appropriate patient selection, distinction between pathologic hypogonadism and functional or age-associated low testosterone, mapping of each recommendation to its evidentiary tier, and close multidisciplinary collaboration.

score.why_it_matters: Provides a contemporary, nuanced synthesis of post-TRAVERSE cardiovascular safety data and regulatory shifts regarding testosterone replacement therapy.
score.bottom_line: While mid-term transdermal testosterone appears noninferior for MACE in selected hypogonadal men, low testosterone remains primarily a marker of multimorbidity, and risks such as blood pressure elevation and unresolved signals for atrial fibrillation warrant cautious, individualized prescription.

title: Intra-Arterial Alteplase After Successful Endovascular Reperfusion in Patients Without Intravenous Thrombolysis: A Subgroup Analysis of the PEARL Randomized Clinical Trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: For patients with large-vessel occlusion stroke who undergo endovascular thrombectomy without prior intravenous thrombolysis, the efficacy and safety of adjunctive intra-arterial alteplase (IAA) after successful endovascular reperfusion remain uncertain.
METHODS: This was a prespecified subgroup analysis of the PEARL (Intra-Arterial Alteplase After Successful Endovascular Reperfusion in Acute Stroke) randomized clinical trial conducted at 28 centers in China, focusing on patients who underwent endovascular thrombectomy without prior intravenous thrombolysis. Patients were stratified by treatment assignment: IAA treatment versus standard treatment (control). The primary efficacy outcome was the proportion of patients achieving excellent functional outcome, defined as a modified Rankin Scale score of 0 to 1 at 90 days. Safety outcomes included symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage, any intracranial hemorrhage within 36 hours, and 90-day all-cause mortality.
RESULTS: Among 324 patients originally randomized in the PEARL trial, 189 underwent endovascular thrombectomy without prior intravenous thrombolysis and were included in this analysis. Of the 189 patients, 95 were assigned to the IAA treatment group and 94 to the standard treatment group. Excellent functional outcome at 90 days was significantly higher in the IAA treatment group compared with the standard treatment group (43.2% [41/95] versus 22.6% [21/93]; adjusted risk ratio [aRR], 1.86; 95% CI, 1.19-2.91; P=0.007). The absolute risk reduction was 20.6% (95% CI, 7.0%-33.1%). Results were consistent in per-protocol sensitivity analyses (P=0.002). No significant differences were observed in symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (aRR, 0.93; 95% CI, 0.28-3.13; P=0.908), any intracranial hemorrhage (aRR, 1.04; 95% CI, 0.68-1.60; P=0.843), or 90-day mortality (hazard ratio [HR], 1.00; 95% CI, 0.49-2.04; P>0.99).
CONCLUSIONS: In patients who did not receive prior intravenous thrombolysis, adjunctive IAA after successful endovascular thrombectomy was associated with a higher likelihood of excellent functional outcome at 90 days, without an apparent increase in symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage or mortality.
REGISTRATION: URL: clinicaltrials.gov; Unique Identifier: NCT05856851.

score.why_it_matters: This subgroup analysis suggests that adjunctive intra-arterial alteplase improves 90-day functional recovery after successful thrombectomy in acute ischemic stroke patients who did not receive IV thrombolysis.
score.bottom_line: In large-vessel occlusion stroke without prior intravenous thrombolysis, adjunctive intra-arterial alteplase post-successful thrombectomy significantly increased excellent 90-day functional outcomes without increasing bleeding complications. As a neurointerventional subgroup analysis, it has limited direct relevance to everyday cardiology practice.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Pharmacologic Therapies in Nonobstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: A Systematic Review.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nonobstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) affects approximately one-third of all patients with HCM and carries substantial morbidity, yet no approved disease-modifying therapies exist. We conducted a systematic review of prospective interventional studies evaluating pharmacologic therapies in adults with nonobstructive HCM.
METHODS: A systematic search of PubMed, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and Clinicaltrials.gov was performed through September 2025. Eligible studies included randomized and nonrandomized prospective interventional trials. A narrative synthesis was performed by pharmacologic class and outcome domain.
RESULTS: Twenty-nine clinical trials evaluating 9 pharmacologic classes were identified: cardiac myosin inhibitors, cardiac sarcomere modulators, metabolic modulators, angiotensin II receptor blockers, angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists, SGLT2 (sodium-glucose cotransporter 2) inhibitors, beta blockers, and calcium channel blockers. Cardiac myosin inhibitors demonstrated reductions in left ventricular hypertrophy, improvements in diastolic function, and marked reductions in cardiac biomarkers, although improvements in exercise capacity and symptoms were variable. SGLT2 inhibition showed concordant improvements in diastolic function, atrial remodeling, biomarkers, and functional status in patients with symptomatic nonobstructive HCM and comorbid type 2 diabetes. Angiotensin receptor blockade showed signals of structural remodeling with valsartan and candesartan without consistent functional benefit. Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonism and angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibition demonstrated largely neutral effects. Among metabolic modulators, ninerafaxstat improved ventilatory efficiency and quality of life in patients with greater baseline symptom burden.
CONCLUSIONS: Pharmacologic responsiveness in nonobstructive HCM is variable and appears to be mechanism- and disease stage-dependent. Ongoing trials evaluating cardiac myosin inhibitors, SGLT inhibitors, and novel therapeutic agents including ninerafaxstat and EDG-7500 will be critical in further defining the therapeutic landscape.

score.why_it_matters: Provides a comprehensive overview of pharmacotherapies in nonobstructive HCM, where disease-modifying options remain absent despite active trial landscapes.
score.bottom_line: Cardiac myosin inhibitors and SGLT2 inhibitors show favorable effects on left ventricular hypertrophy and biomarkers, but functional improvements in nonobstructive HCM remain inconsistent pending ongoing phase 3 trials.

title: Macrophage-Derived Glycoprotein Nonmetastatic Melanoma Protein B Attenuates Cardiac Dysfunction by Promoting Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor-Independent Angiogenesis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pressure overload-induced heart failure involves maladaptive cardiac remodeling and inadequate angiogenesis. The limitations of VEGF (vascular endothelial growth factor)-based therapies underscore the need to identify alternative angiogenic pathways. GPNMB (glycoprotein nonmetastatic melanoma protein B) is a macrophage-secreted protein implicated in tissue repair, but its role in pressure overload-induced cardiac remodeling and its potential to modulate angiogenesis remain unknown.
METHODS: Myeloid-specific Gpnmb knockout and control mice were subjected to transverse aortic constriction. Cardiac function, remodeling, and capillary density were assessed. Single-cell RNA sequencing was performed to identify transcriptomic changes. In vitro, human endothelial cells were treated with recombinant GPNMB to assess proliferation, migration, and tube formation, and to dissect the underlying signaling pathways. The therapeutic potential of Gpnmb overexpression was evaluated using AAV9 vectors.
RESULTS: Myeloid Gpnmb deletion exacerbated transverse aortic constriction-induced cardiac dysfunction, hypertrophy, fibrosis, and capillary rarefaction. Single-cell sequencing revealed a reduced capillary endothelial cell population and pathway enrichment indicative of endothelial dysfunction and metabolic reprogramming in myeloid-specific Gpnmb knockout hearts. Mechanistically, GPNMB directly promoted endothelial cell proliferation, migration, and tube formation by activating the mTOR (mechanistic target of rapamycin) pathway in a CD44-dependent manner, independently of VEGF signaling. Cardiac-specific Gpnmb overexpression rescued angiogenesis, improved cardiac function, and attenuated pathological remodeling after transverse aortic constriction.
CONCLUSIONS: Macrophage-derived GPNMB is a critical regulator of cardiac adaptation to pressure overload. It promotes a VEGF-independent angiogenic program probably via the CD44/mTOR axis, as supported by in vitro mechanistic studies. GPNMB represents a promising therapeutic target for heart failure characterized by microvascular rarefaction.

score.why_it_matters: This preclinical study identifies macrophage-derived GPNMB as an alternative, VEGF-independent driver of cardiac angiogenesis that mitigates pressure-overload remodeling in mice.
score.bottom_line: Targeting GPNMB may represent a future therapeutic avenue to counteract microvascular rarefaction in pressure-overload heart failure, but human clinical relevance remains to be established.

title: Targeting Mediator Kinase Attenuates Cardiac Hypertrophy by Regulating Enhancer Utilization.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac hypertrophy is characterized by extensive transcriptional remodeling that contributes to the progression of heart failure. Preclinical models demonstrate that therapies targeting hypertrophic responses can mitigate disease severity. Recent evidence shows that failing human and murine hearts exhibit elevated mediator kinase expression, sufficient to drive eccentric hypertrophy and heart failure through activation of hypertrophic gene programs. Mediator kinase inhibition suppresses oncogenic transcription by altering enhancer utilization, suggesting similar mechanisms may attenuate pathological remodeling in the heart. This study investigates whether mediator kinase inhibition can blunt cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, offering a potential therapeutic strategy for heart failure.
METHODS: Two structurally unrelated mediator kinase inhibitors, Senexin A (SxnA) and CCT251545, were tested in neonatal rat cardiomyocytes. Hypertrophy was assessed by cell size measurements, RNA sequencing, and H3K27ac chromatin immunoprecipitation sequencing.
RESULTS: Mediator kinase inhibition significantly reduced hypertrophic growth, attenuating cell size increases induced by phenylephrine (PE) and endothelin-1. Transcriptomic profiling revealed a dose-dependent suppression of PE-induced differentially expressed genes in Senexin A-treated cells. Mechanistically, PE stimulation enhanced RNA polymerase II pause release, whereas Mediator kinase inhibition did not alter this process. Epigenomic analysis showed that PE markedly increased the number of super-enhancers relative to vehicle treatment, while co-treatment with Senexin A reduced the total number of active enhancers. Nearest-neighbor analysis linked putative regulatory enhancers to key PE-responsive genes, and these enhancer signatures were blunted by SxnA.
CONCLUSIONS: These findings demonstrate that Mediator kinase inhibition counteracts hypertrophic growth and transcriptional reprogramming, highlighting its potential as a therapeutic strategy to modulate pathological gene regulation in cardiac hypertrophy.

score.why_it_matters: This study identifies mediator kinase inhibition as an epigenetic mechanism to suppress transcriptional reprogramming and hypertrophy in cardiomyocyte models.
score.bottom_line: In vitro inhibition of mediator kinase reduced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and super-enhancer activation, identifying a potential early preclinical target for future heart failure therapeutics.

title: Integrative Genomic Analyses Identify Collagen Type XXI Alpha 1 Chain and ENPEP-Fibroblast Growth Factor 5 Regulatory Pathways for Blood Pressure Variation in East Asian People.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension and diabetes are common cardiometabolic disorders that may share genetic and environmental risk factors. However, the regulatory genes and tissue-specific mechanisms underlying blood pressure variations remain incompletely understood.
METHODS: Leveraging a well-characterized prospective population-based cohort comprised of 27 308 participants from the SCHS (Singapore Chinese Health Study), we evaluated genome-wide genetic associations for 5 blood pressure traits: hypertension status, systolic blood pressure, diastolic blood pressure, mean arterial pressure and pulse pressure. Additionally, we conducted a transcriptome-wide association study, integrating gene expression data from 49 tissues, followed by colocalization and fine-mapping to prioritize regulatory genes. Association of identified variants with incident diabetes was additionally evaluated in the longitudinal data.
RESULTS: We validated 10 blood pressure loci (P between 1.64×10-20-4.10×10-8) and identified an East Asian-specific splice donor variant at the COL21A1 gene associated with pulse pressure (rs149344559, P=6.78×10-10). Integrative analyses prioritized FGF5 in kidney cortex and ENPEP in pituitary tissue as candidate regulatory genes. The blood pressure-lowering allele at ENPEP (T allele, rs1879056) was associated with reduced risk of incident diabetes. Mediation analysis demonstrated that ∼20.1% of the genetic association with diabetes was mediated through mean arterial pressure (Pindirect-effect<0.001).
CONCLUSIONS: This study refines genetic predispositions for blood pressure among East Asian individuals. We further delineate tissue-specific regulatory pathways underlying blood pressure variations and identify ENPEP-mediated dysfunctions linking blood pressure genetics to diabetes risk, underscoring integrated disease mechanisms.

score.why_it_matters: Identifies East Asian-specific genetic loci (COL21A1, ENPEP, FGF5) linking blood pressure regulation to diabetes risk, offering mechanistic insights but no immediate bedside utility.
score.bottom_line: Integrative genomic analyses highlight tissue-specific pathways linking hypertension and incident diabetes in East Asian individuals. These findings are foundational for target discovery but have no current impact on clinical management.

title: Assessment of Persistent Postpartum Hypertension Following Hypertensive Disorders of Pregnancy: A Scoping Review.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Identifying individuals with persistent postpartum hypertension (ppHTN) after hypertensive disorders of pregnancy is an important strategy to mitigate associated long-term cardiovascular risks. Accordingly, we aimed to review the literature surrounding the assessment of ppHTN after hypertensive disorders of pregnancy.
METHODS: We conducted a scoping review using Arksey and O'Malley's methodological framework. We developed and pilot-tested a data extraction tool to collect information on ppHTN assessment methods, including timing and setting, blood pressure (BP) thresholds used, and inclusion of patient preferences. Data were synthesized into tables and narrative summaries. Barriers and facilitators to BP assessment protocols, remote BP monitoring, and follow-up attendance were mapped using the Capability, Opportunity, and Motivation - Behavior (COM-B) framework.
RESULTS: Of 14 593 records, 96 papers met inclusion criteria. BP measured in the hospital alone was most common (n=41), followed by the hospital/home combination (n=18), and the outpatient/home combination (n=9). Monitoring typically began within 0 to 7 days postpartum (n=28), ending at 1 to 6 weeks (n=20) or 6 to 12 months (n=20) postpartum. ppHTN was defined using elevated BP thresholds (n=28), most commonly ≥140/90 mm Hg (n=18), medication initiation (n=8), lack of BP normalization over time (n=4), or referral to a specialist (n=2). Only 7 studies assessed patient preferences. Facilitators to home BP assessment included the use of educational material, while barriers involved digital access limitations.
CONCLUSIONS: ppHTN assessment methods varied in timing, setting, and BP thresholds. Findings underscore the need for standardized, patient-centered guidelines that account for BP assessment methods across settings.

score.why_it_matters: It highlights widespread heterogeneity in how persistent postpartum hypertension is monitored and defined, emphasizing the urgent need for standardized post-pregnancy surveillance protocols.
score.bottom_line: Postpartum blood pressure monitoring varies widely in duration, setting, and diagnostic thresholds (though ≥140/90 mm Hg is most frequent). Clinicians should proactively organize structured home or outpatient blood pressure follow-up beyond the immediate hospital discharge period for women with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy.

title: Anthracycline Cardiotoxicity as Multicellular Network Failure: Cardiac Niche Reprogramming and Pathological Cell-Cell Communication.
abstract: Anthracyclines are essential anticancer agents, yet a cardiomyocyte-centered model incompletely explains why cardiac injury can be delayed, progressive, and poorly captured by resting ejection fraction. We frame anthracycline cardiotoxicity as a multicellular network failure within the cardiac niche: the spatially organized interactions among cardiomyocytes, fibroblasts, endothelial and immune cells, extracellular matrix, and circulating signals. Cardiomyocyte stress initiates injury, whereas pathological communication may propagate it. We distinguish a fibroblast-CD8+ T-cell adhesion circuit, supported by loss-of-function evidence in mice and correlative human data, from an emerging therapy-conditioned tumor-heart extracellular vesicle axis supported mainly by breast cancer models. These pathways may converge on fibrotic stiffness, microvascular dysfunction, and electrical uncoupling; however, direct cross-circuit interaction and drug-independent sufficiency remain unproven. We integrate established clinical risk modifiers with this framework, specify causal criteria, and propose spatial multiomics, living myocardial slices, tumor-bearing systems, and longitudinal phenotyping to test circuit persistence. This evidence-calibrated model shifts the goal from cataloging cell-intrinsic pathways to identifying mechanism-resolved biomarkers and therapeutically targetable communication nodes while preserving antitumor efficacy.

score.why_it_matters: It proposes a conceptual shift in anthracycline cardiotoxicity from purely cell-intrinsic cardiomyocyte injury to a multicellular cardiac niche failure involving fibroblasts, immune cells, and extracellular vesicles.
score.bottom_line: This mechanistic review highlights novel translational targets in non-cardiomyocyte cellular networks, but it has no immediate impact on clinical cardio-oncology practice or screening protocols.

title: Baseline Characteristics, Geriatric Syndromes, and Clinical Outcomes During Implementation of a Cardiovascular Center on Aging.

score.why_it_matters: Evaluates the implementation of a dedicated geriatric cardiology program to identify frailty and geriatric syndromes in older cardiovascular patients.
score.bottom_line: Descriptive institutional report on incorporating geriatric assessments into cardiovascular care; provides operational insight but does not alter standard management guidelines.

title: Plasminogen Activator Inhibitor-1 Deficiency Exacerbates Pressure Overload-Induced Cardiac Hypertrophy in Mice.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pathological cardiac hypertrophy is a key precursor to heart failure. PAI-1 (plasminogen activator inhibitor-1) is a recognized profibrotic mediator, yet its role in the heart remains paradoxical and incompletely understood.
METHODS: Six-week-old male wild-type (PAI-1+/+) and PAI-1 knockout (PAI-1-/-) mice underwent sham or transverse aortic constriction surgery, followed by assessment of cardiac morphology, molecular markers, and function. In H9C2 cardiomyocytes, PAI-1 was silenced or overexpressed before angiotensin II stimulation, with or without targeted signaling inhibitors, followed by coimmunoprecipitation, Western blotting, and immunofluorescence.
RESULTS: Pressure overload increased plasma and myocardial PAI-1 levels. PAI-1 deficiency exacerbated transverse aortic constriction-induced cardiac dysfunction, hypertrophy, and fibrosis, accompanied by JAK2/STAT3 (Janus kinase 2/signal transducer and activator of transcription 3) activation and collagen overexpression, whereas cardiac-specific overexpression attenuated these maladaptive changes. Moreover, STAT3 inhibition reversed the adverse cardiac remodeling associated with PAI-1 deletion. In vitro, PAI-1 knockdown potentiated angiotensin II-induced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, an effect that was rescued by PAI-1 overexpression. Mechanistically, PAI-1 associated with JAK2 and STAT3, with reduced phosphorylation of both proteins and impaired STAT3 nuclear translocation. Critically, pharmacological inhibition of STAT3 abolished the harmful effects of PAI-1 silencing.
CONCLUSIONS: PAI-1 acts as an endogenous cardioprotective checkpoint by negatively regulating JAK2/STAT3 signaling. These findings suggest a noncanonical cardiomyocyte-associated function of PAI-1 beyond its classical fibrinolytic role and identify the PAI-1-JAK2/STAT3 axis as a potential therapeutic target for heart failure with hypertrophy.

score.why_it_matters: Provides preclinical mechanistic insight into how PAI-1 unexpectedly restrains pathological cardiac hypertrophy via negative regulation of the JAK2/STAT3 pathway.
score.bottom_line: In mouse models of pressure overload, PAI-1 deficiency worsens adverse remodeling, highlighting a noncanonical cardioprotective role that has no immediate impact on clinical practice.

title: Greater Neighborhood Resources Predict Reduced In-Hospital Death for Children With Heart Failure and Cardiomyopathy.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with pediatric heart failure (HF) face significant morbidity and death. However, there are limited data describing neighborhood characteristics in pediatric patients with HF or exploring the relationship of these factors to resource use and clinical outcomes. We used the Child Opportunity Index 3.0 (COI), a composite index of community resources pertinent to child health, to describe neighborhood characteristics for children with HF and identify its associations with in-hospital death.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used the Pediatric Health Information System, a national administrative database of tertiary care pediatric hospitals. Inpatient encounters between January 2014 and December 2024 for pediatric patients (aged <18 years) with HF and cardiomyopathy were identified using International Classification of Diseases (ICD) codes. The primary exposure of interest was the COI, and the primary outcome of interest was in-hospital death. Mixed logistic regression models were estimated, unadjusted and adjusted for administrative sex, age, race, and primary payor.
RESULTS: Our cohort consisted of index HF admissions in 7060 patients. Half of the cohort was in either the very low (n=2034 [29%]) or low (n=1521 [22%]) COI quintile. After adjustment, patients with a very high COI were less likely to experience in-hospital death than those living in very low COI neighborhoods (odds ratio, 0.73 [95% CI, 0.54-0.99]; P=0.048).
CONCLUSIONS: A substantial proportion of children admitted with HF have limited neighborhood resources. Those with higher neighborhood resources are more likely to survive to discharge, emphasizing the relationship between environmental factors and clinical outcomes in pediatric HF.

score.why_it_matters: Demonstrates that neighborhood-level social determinants of health independently correlate with in-hospital mortality among children admitted with heart failure and cardiomyopathy.
score.bottom_line: In pediatric heart failure admissions, patients from areas with higher neighborhood resources had significantly lower in-hospital mortality compared to those from very low-resource communities. Clinicians should recognize that adverse social determinants of health are tied to worse inpatient outcomes in this vulnerable population.

title: Combined Prognostic Value of Cardiac Magnetic Resonance-Derived Myocardial Extracellular Volume and the Fibrosis-4 Index in Patients With Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction is increasingly recognized as a multisystem metabolic-inflammatory syndrome. We investigated the comparative and complementary prognostic value of cardiac magnetic resonance-derived extracellular volume fraction (ECV) and the Fibrosis-4 index for predicting adverse cardiovascular outcomes in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.
METHODS: Between 2017 and 2019, 250 patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction underwent assessment of myocardial ECV by cardiac magnetic resonance and hepatic fibrosis using the Fibrosis-4 index. The primary outcome was a composite of cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization. Multivariable Cox regression and discrimination analyses were performed to evaluate prognostic performance.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 1190 days, 75 patients (30.0%) experienced the primary outcome. Both ECV (hazard ratio [HR], 1.13 [95% CI, 1.08-1.17]; P<0.001) and the Fibrosis-4 index (HR, 1.12 [95% CI, 1.02-1.22]; P=0.015) independently predicted the primary outcome. Patients with concomitantly elevated ECV and Fibrosis-4 index had a markedly increased risk of adverse events compared with those with low values of both markers. ECV-based models demonstrated superior discrimination compared with Fibrosis-4-based models (concordance index, 0.732 versus 0.663; P=0.011). Addition of ECV to the Fibrosis-4 model significantly improved discrimination, whereas addition of the Fibrosis-4 index to the ECV model improved reclassification (continuous net reclassification improvement and integrated discrimination improvement) but not discrimination.
CONCLUSIONS: Both myocardial ECV and the Fibrosis-4 index independently predict adverse cardiovascular outcomes in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction. Although ECV provides greater prognostic discrimination, combined assessment of ECV and the Fibrosis-4 index identifies a subgroup at particularly high risk and may provide complementary information for risk stratification.

score.why_it_matters: Demonstrates that multiorgan fibrotic remodeling, reflected by myocardial extracellular volume on CMR and hepatic FIB-4 index, offers incremental prognostic value in HFpEF.
score.bottom_line: In patients with HFpEF, both CMR-derived ECV and the liver-derived FIB-4 index independently predict adverse cardiovascular events. Concomitant elevation of both markers identifies an especially high-risk phenotype, though clinical management remains unchanged based on these metrics alone.

title: Neuropsychological and Quality-of-Life Outcomes After Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Survivors of aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage often have long-term neuropsychological disturbances. This study aims to characterize depressive symptoms, quality of life, and personality changes in a large cohort of survivors of aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage.
METHODS: This cross-sectional study included patients with a history of aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage from the Brain Aneurysm Foundation patient registry. Patients completed the Beck Depression Inventory-II and the Stroke-Specific Quality of Life scale, and family members completed the Iowa Scales of Personality Change. Multiple linear regression was used to identify symptoms associated with reduced work productivity. Wilcoxon and chi-square tests were used to identify variables associated with severity of depressive symptoms and personality changes.
RESULTS: A total of 318 patients were included, with 242 completing the Beck Depression Inventory-II and Stroke-Specific Quality of Life, and 112 family members completing the Iowa Scales of Personality Change.
