Moderate depressive symptoms were reported by 18% of patients, and severe symptoms were reported by 11%. Impairments in thinking, social roles, language, and energy were independently associated with reduced work productivity. Acquired personality disturbances were observed in 72% of patients for executive function, 44% for social behavior, 49% for hypomotivation, 50% for irascibility, and 72% for distress. Ruptured aneurysms in the anterior cerebral and anterior communicating artery were associated with a trend toward a higher prevalence of moderate to severe depressive symptoms and executive personality changes.
CONCLUSIONS: Depressive symptoms and personality changes are common after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage, affecting work productivity. Recognizing challenges in thinking, social interactions, language, and vulnerability to pressure may help guide targeted interventions by families, employers, and health care providers.

score.why_it_matters: Survivors of aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage experience high rates of enduring personality changes, depressive symptoms, and cognitive deficits that impair quality of life and work productivity.
score.bottom_line: Nearly 30% of aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage survivors report moderate-to-severe depressive symptoms, and the majority exhibit acquired executive and distress-related personality changes. Long-term neurocognitive follow-up and targeted multidisciplinary support are essential during recovery.

title: Plasma Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme as a Prioritized Candidate Target for Alzheimer's Disease: Evidence From Proteome-Wide Mendelian Randomization and a Large Prospective Cohort Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: We aimed to provide hypothesis-generating evidence on druggable targets for Alzheimer's disease (AD) by integrating proteome-wide Mendelian randomization (MR) with evidence from a conventional observational analysis of drug use in a large prospective cohort.
METHODS: Proteome-wide MR analysis was conducted to identify plasma proteins causally related to AD risk using the largest summary-level data to date, followed by colocalization and multiomic validation analyses (on the gene expression, alternative splicing, and DNA methylation levels in blood and brain, respectively) to prioritize potential druggable targets. We also replicated our MR findings using additional genetic data and performed multivariable MR for the prioritized findings. Conventional observational analysis in UK Biobank, a large prospective cohort, was performed to provide further clinical implications, using active comparator to minimize confounding by indication.
RESULTS: MR analysis identified 15 plasma proteins with putative causal effects on AD risk. Of them, inhibition of angiotensin-converting enzyme was found to increase the risk of AD (odds ratio, 1.10 [95% CI, 1.08-1.14]), which was likely independent of blood pressure as suggested by multivariable MR. Observational analysis in UK Biobank showed a higher incidence (hazard ratio, 1.23 [95% CI, 1.00-1.50]) of AD among regular users of angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors, compared with the active comparator angiotensin receptor blocker users.
CONCLUSIONS: Our genetic analyses prioritized angiotensin-converting enzyme as a candidate target, and a conventional observational analysis in a large prospective cohort provided supportive evidence that regular angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor use was associated with a higher AD risk, which needs further investigation with high-quality real-world evidence and clinical trials before being translated into practice changes.

score.why_it_matters: This study combines Mendelian randomization with UK Biobank data to suggest that ACE inhibition may be causally linked to a slightly increased risk of Alzheimer's disease compared with ARB use.
score.bottom_line: While hypothesis-generating and supportive of ARBs over ACE inhibitors regarding neurocognitive outcomes, these findings do not warrant immediate changes to standard guideline-directed antihypertensive or heart failure regimens without randomized trial confirmation.

title: PASCAL Precision System Outcomes by Implant Location and Lesion Location in Degenerative Mitral Regurgitation Patients From the STS/ACC TVT Registry.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair can be more challenging in noncentral regions of the valve and in anterior or bileaflet lesions. We assess effect of implant location and leaflet lesion location on safety and effectiveness of PASCAL Precision system in degenerative mitral regurgitation (MR).
METHODS: Mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair outcomes in patients with degenerative MR treated with PASCAL Precision system (September 2022-October 2024), from the US STS/ACC TVT (Society of Thoracic Surgeons/American College of Cardiology Transcatheter Valve Therapy) Registry, were analyzed by implant location (A2P2/non-A2P2) and leaflet lesion location (anterior/posterior/bileaflet). Procedural, clinical, and echocardiographic outcomes to 30 days were assessed.
RESULTS: At 30 days, both A2P2 (n=1526) and non-A2P2 (n=299) groups had low event rates (cardiovascular mortality: 1.1% versus 1.0%, mitral valve reintervention: 0.4% versus 0.0% and single leaflet device attachment: 0.5% versus 0.3%; all P>0.05) and demonstrated significant MR reduction (P<0.001 versus baseline) with no significant difference between groups (P=0.750) (MR ≤2+: 93.4% versus 95.4%; MR ≤1+: 72.0% versus 73.3%). Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary scores improved significantly in both groups (∆19.3, ∆17.7 points; P=0.741). The anterior (n=250), posterior (n=902), and bileaflet (n=192) disease groups also had low event rates (cardiovascular mortality: 0.4%, 1.1%, 0.0%; mitral valve reintervention: 0.8%, 0.1%, 0.5%; and single leaflet device attachment: 0.8%, 0.2%, 0.5%; all P>0.05), and demonstrated significant MR reduction (P<0.001 versus baseline) with no significant difference across groups (P=0.459) (MR ≤2+: 94.1%, 93.1%, and 94.5%; MR ≤1+: 79.0%, 69.2%, and 72.4%). All groups experienced significant improvement in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary scores (∆21.4, ∆18.8, ∆12.0 points; P=0.087).
CONCLUSION: In real-world patients with degenerative mitral regurgitation, treatment with the PASCAL Precision system was associated with favorable safety and effectiveness at 30 days, regardless of implant location or leaflet lesion location.

score.why_it_matters: Real-world registry data confirm that transcatheter edge-to-edge repair with the PASCAL Precision system achieves comparable 30-day safety and MR reduction even in anatomically challenging non-A2P2, anterior, or bileaflet degenerative lesions.
score.bottom_line: In this large TVT Registry analysis of degenerative MR, PASCAL Precision demonstrated high technical success (MR ≤2+ in >93%) and low complication rates at 30 days regardless of implant location or leaflet lesion anatomy. This supports expanding TEER consideration beyond strictly central A2-P2 pathology.

title: Evaluation of Acute Electrical and Hemodynamic Improvement During Left Bundle-Branch Area Pacing Modalities for Resynchronization Therapy.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: While cardiac resynchronization therapy is effective in dyssynchronous heart failure, suboptimal response remains frequent. The acute hemodynamic profile of different left bundle-branch (LBB) area pacing modalities is poorly defined. Moreover, atrioventricular optimization guided by QRS duration (QRSd) may not yield the greatest hemodynamic benefit.
METHODS: Twenty-four patients with heart failure, reduced ejection fraction, and LBB block underwent sequential testing of right ventricular septal pacing, left ventricular septal pacing, nonselective LBB pacing, and selective LBB pacing during cardiac resynchronization therapy implantation in a prospective, within-subject physiological study. At each modality, electrical end points were QRSd and vectorcardiographic QRS area; hemodynamics were assessed with beat-to-beat systolic blood pressure (SBP). The atrioventricular interval producing maximal SBP improvement was compared with that producing the narrowest QRSd.
RESULTS: LBB area pacing modalities significantly reduced QRSd, compared with right ventricular septal pacing (nonselective LBB pacing, 114.0±16.8 milliseconds; selective LBB pacing, 118.4±14.1 milliseconds; left ventricular septal pacing, 124.6±16.0 milliseconds; right ventricular septal pacing, 144.4±27.6 milliseconds; all P<0.01). At the atrioventricular interval that produced maximized SBP improvement, QRSd remained narrower with LBB area pacing than right ventricular septal pacing, and selective LBB pacing provided the greatest hemodynamic improvement (ΔSBP 16.3±5.2 mm Hg), exceeding left ventricular septal pacing (13.5±6.2 mm Hg) and nonselective LBB pacing (12.8±6.3 mm Hg; all P<0.05). Across modalities, the atrioventricular interval that maximized ΔSBP was consistently shorter than that minimizing QRSd (mean difference, 18-29 milliseconds).
CONCLUSIONS: Selective LBB pacing yields the greatest acute hemodynamic benefit, and the hemodynamic-optimal atrioventricular interval is shorter than the electrical-optimal atrioventricular interval, suggesting that modest atrioventricular interval shortening after electrical optimization may better maximize hemodynamics.
REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique Identifier: NCT07032064.

score.why_it_matters: Provides mechanistic insight into conduction system pacing, demonstrating that selective left bundle-branch pacing confers the greatest acute hemodynamic gain and that optimal atrioventricular timing may differ from pure QRS minimization.
score.bottom_line: In patients undergoing resynchronization with left bundle-branch area pacing, selective pacing provided superior acute systolic blood pressure improvements compared with nonselective or LV septal pacing. Hemodynamic optimization required slightly shorter atrioventricular intervals than those that produced the narrowest QRS duration.

title: Implementation of a WatchPAT-Based Diagnostic Pathway for Obstructive Sleep Apnea in a Tertiary Hypertension Center: A Feasibility Study.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a prevalent yet underdiagnosed in hypertension, affecting 30% to 83% of patients. Limited polysomnography access delays diagnosis. We evaluated the feasibility, diagnostic yield, and downstream management decisions of an integrated diagnostic pathway using WatchPAT 300, a peripheral arterial tonometry-based home sleep apnea test, in a tertiary hypertension unit.
METHODS: In this single-center, prospective, observational study, 200 patients underwent ambulatory OSA assessment from May 2023 through August 2025. We recorded clinical variables, peripheral arterial tonometry data, and management decisions. A subgroup underwent confirmatory in-laboratory polysomnography. Patients were classified as none-to-mild OSA (peripheral apneahypopnea index <15/h) and moderate-to-severe OSA (≥15/h).
RESULTS: The pathway achieved 97.5% (95% CI, 94%-99%) technical success and reduced the mean time-to-diagnosis to 3.5±4.5 days, versus 154 days for in-laboratory polysomnography. Over half of the cohort was triaged: ∼30% met treatment criteria directly, and 22% were ruled out. Among patients completing confirmatory polysomnography, 83% (95% CI, 61%-94%) initially classified as none-to-mild were reclassified as moderate-to-severe OSA, and 77% required treatment. Furthermore, symptoms were dissociated from severity, and Snoring-Tired-Observed-Pressure-BMI-Age-Gender (STOP-Bag) association with severity did not remain significant after multiplicity correction.
CONCLUSIONS: A peripheral arterial tonometry-based home sleep apnea test-first model is feasible and efficient, eliminating diagnostic delays. Although effective for triaging clear-cut cases, the high reclassification rate underscores the almost mandatory role of confirmatory polysomnography for milder or equivocal results, suspected comorbid sleep disorders, or high STOP-Bag score. These data argue against symptoms-based screening alone to screen populations with hypertension.

score.why_it_matters: Demonstrates the feasibility of rapid home sleep apnea triage in a hypertension clinic while highlighting a concerningly high rate of underdiagnosis for mild cases compared to polysomnography.
score.bottom_line: A WatchPAT-first diagnostic pathway drastically shortens time to obstructive sleep apnea diagnosis in hypertension clinics, but high reclassification rates mean negative or mild findings still require confirmatory polysomnography.

title: Nuclear Factor Kappa-B Inducing Kinase- and Inhibitor of Nuclear Factor Kappa-B Kinase Subunit Beta-Binding Protein Promotes Pathological Cardiac Hypertrophy by Regulating Inhibitor of Nuclear Factor Kappa-B Kinase Subunit Beta-Mediated Nuclear Factor Kappa-B Activation.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pathological cardiac hypertrophy is a major risk factor for heart failure. NIBP (NF-κB [nuclear factor kappa-B] inducing kinase- and inhibitor of NF-κB kinase subunit beta-binding protein) is a key regulator of cytokine-induced NF-κB signaling, but its role in cardiac hypertrophy remains unknown.
METHODS: We established transverse aortic constriction-induced cardiac hypertrophy in mice and phenylephrine-induced hypertrophy in neonatal rat ventricular myocytes. Genetic interventions included generation of whole-body Nibp knockout mice via CRISPR-Cas9; creation of cardiomyocyte-specific Nibp knockout mice using adeno-associated virus serotype 9-delivered Cre and single-guide RNAs in Rosa26-LSL-Cas9 mice; and cardiac-specific Nibp overexpression via adeno-associated virus serotype 9delivery. In neonatal rat ventricular myocytes, NIBP was knocked down or overexpressed using adenoviruses. Phenotypes were assessed by echocardiography, histology (wheat germ agglutinin, picrosirius redstaining), and molecular analyses. Mechanisms were investigated via RNA-sequencing, coimmunoprecipitation, and Western blotting for key signaling molecules.
RESULTS: NIBP protein was upregulated in hypertrophic hearts and cardiomyocytes. Both Nibp-knockout and cardiomyocyte-specific Nibp knockout attenuated transverse aortic constriction-induced cardiac dysfunction, hypertrophy, and fibrosis, whereas Nibp overexpression exacerbated these pathologies. Consistently, in neonatal rat ventricular myocytes, NIBP knockdown mitigated, while its overexpression aggravated, phenylephrine-induced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and inflammatory responses. Mechanistically, NIBP directly interacted with IKKβ (inhibitor of NF-κB kinase subunit beta), enhanced its phosphorylation, and drove hyperactivation of the downstream NF-κB pathway. Overexpression of a kinase-dead IKKβ mutant reversed the hypertrophic effects of NIBP.
CONCLUSIONS: NIBP promotes pathological cardiac hypertrophy by activating the IKKβ/NF-κB axis, identifying it as a potential therapeutic target for cardiac remodeling and heart failure.

score.why_it_matters: Identifies NIBP as a molecular regulator of cardiac hypertrophy and remodeling via the IKKβ/NF-κB pathway in preclinical rodent models.
score.bottom_line: This basic science investigation demonstrates that NIBP promotes pressure-overload cardiac hypertrophy in mice, highlighting a novel mechanistic pathway with distant translational potential.

title: Polarimetric Imaging: In Search for Clinically Meaningful Vulnerability.

score.why_it_matters: Provides expert commentary on the evolving role and clinical challenges of polarimetric intracoronary imaging for identifying vulnerable atherosclerotic plaques.
score.bottom_line: Polarimetric imaging offers novel tissue-characterization capabilities for assessing plaque microarchitecture, but its translation into improved clinical outcomes remains under investigation.

title: Guidelines on rehabilitation and a focus on lifestyle-related cardiovascular prevention.

score.why_it_matters: Editorial issue overview highlighting recent guideline developments and focus areas in cardiovascular rehabilitation and lifestyle prevention.
score.bottom_line: This article serves as an introductory editorial or issue summary rather than a standalone clinical practice guideline. Clinicians should refer directly to the full ESC Guidelines for specific clinical recommendations.

title: Concomitant Balloon-in-Basket Pulsed Field Ablation and Next-Generation Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion: Acute Procedural Success and Early Safety and Effectiveness results from the Prospective Multicenter CLEAR Study.

score.why_it_matters: Evaluates the feasibility and acute safety of combining novel balloon-in-basket pulsed field ablation with left atrial appendage occlusion in a single procedure.
score.bottom_line: Early prospective multicenter data from the CLEAR study suggest that concomitant balloon-in-basket PFA and next-generation LAAO is acutely feasible and safe, though long-term efficacy and randomized comparisons are still needed.

title: Safety, Efficacy and Cost of Same-Day Discharge after Pulsed Field Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation: A Sub-study of the Multicentre SENTINEL Registry.

score.why_it_matters: As pulsed field ablation expands rapidly, evidence supporting same-day discharge helps optimize hospital bed utilization and procedural costs without compromising safety.
score.bottom_line: This SENTINEL registry sub-study provides multicenter real-world evidence supporting the safety, efficacy, and cost-effectiveness of same-day discharge protocols following pulsed field ablation for atrial fibrillation.

title: When platelets are under pressure: an angiotensin II-TGF-β axis in hypertensive patients leads to receptor PAR4 overexpression.

score.why_it_matters: Identifies a mechanistic link between hypertension, the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system, and platelet PAR4 upregulation, highlighting potential future antiplatelet targets.
score.bottom_line: Hypertension-driven angiotensin II and TGF-beta signaling increases platelet PAR4 expression, providing insight into prothrombotic risk in hypertension but without immediate changes to clinical management.

title: A decade-long device-valve interaction: severe aortic regurgitation after residual ventricular septal defect closure.

score.why_it_matters: Illustrates the risk of delayed mechanical complications, specifically aortic valve impingement and severe aortic regurgitation, years after percutaneous VSD device closure.
score.bottom_line: Long-term echocardiographic surveillance of aortic valve function is necessary following VSD device closure due to the potential for late device-leaflet erosion or interaction.

title: Heart failure management and outcomes: what can we learn from Japan?

score.why_it_matters: Provides systemic and epidemiological perspective on differences in heart failure care and patient outcomes between Japan and Western countries.
score.bottom_line: This editorial highlights unique aspects of Japanese heart failure care and epidemiology, but does not provide direct evidence to alter individual clinical management.

title: Beyond tetramer stability: wild-type ATTR-CM as a disease of the ageing myocardium.

score.why_it_matters: Provides a conceptual perspective on wild-type ATTR cardiomyopathy, emphasizing that myocardial aging biology contributes to disease progression beyond just circulating transthyretin tetramer instability.
score.bottom_line: This review frames wild-type ATTR-CM within the broader context of cardiac aging rather than solely as a protein-misfolding disorder. While conceptually illuminating for disease understanding, it does not alter current diagnostic or therapeutic management.

title: The evolution and future of conduction system pacing.
abstract: Cardiac pacing has undergone a fundamental paradigm shift from conventional right ventricular apical pacing towards physiological activation of the native conduction system of the heart. Decades of evidence have established that chronic right ventricular pacing induces ventricular dyssynchrony, contributing to pacing-induced cardiomyopathy and adverse clinical outcomes. Conduction system pacing, which engages the intrinsic His-Purkinje network of the heart, has emerged as a transformative approach that preserves or restores the natural ventricular activation sequence. His bundle pacing, the earliest form of conduction system pacing, provided proof of concept but is limited by technical challenges and high capture thresholds. Left bundle branch area pacing has since become the dominant modality, offering greater procedural success, lead stability and broader applicability: from management of bradycardia and prevention of pacing-induced cardiomyopathy to cardiac resynchronization therapy in heart failure. Bachmann bundle area pacing is an emerging atrial counterpart: by capturing a preferential interatrial conduction pathway, this approach reduces interatrial conduction delay and produces a more physiological atrial activation sequence than conventional right atrial appendage pacing. Bachmann bundle area pacing might, therefore, help to prevent atrial fibrillation. In this Review, we bring these ventricular and atrial strategies together under the unifying principle of physiological pacing, describe their mechanistic basis and technical evolution, appraise the latest evidence from randomized trials and address the practical questions that arise in clinical application, indicating where more evidence is required.

score.why_it_matters: Provides a comprehensive overview of the paradigm shift toward physiological pacing, detailing the rise of left bundle branch area pacing and emerging concepts such as Bachmann bundle pacing.
score.bottom_line: Left bundle branch area pacing has become the dominant physiological pacing approach over His bundle pacing due to superior lead stability and electrical parameters, though ongoing randomized trials are needed to fully define hard outcome benefits across broader indications.

title: Infective endocarditis after transcatheter aortic valve replacement in patients receiving dialysis: risks, outcomes and management.

score.why_it_matters: Dialysis patients undergoing TAVR face disproportionately high risks of infective endocarditis with grim outcomes, requiring vigilant diagnostic and preventive strategies.
score.bottom_line: This review summarizes the epidemiology, diagnostic pitfalls, and management considerations for infective endocarditis following TAVR in patients with end-stage renal disease on dialysis.

title: Distinguishing between nicotine replacement therapies and nicotine-containing consumer products.

score.why_it_matters: Clarifying the distinction between regulated medicinal nicotine replacement therapies and recreational consumer nicotine products is relevant for smoking cessation counseling.
score.bottom_line: This correspondence emphasizes the need to differentiate therapeutic smoking cessation aids from recreational nicotine products, though it provides no new clinical trial data.

title: Targeting the Vein of Marshall in the Modern Era: Do We Still Need Ethanol?

score.why_it_matters: This letter examines whether vein of Marshall ethanol infusion remains necessary alongside advancing catheter ablation technologies like pulsed-field ablation.
score.bottom_line: As modern ablation modalities evolve to achieve reliable mitral isthmus block, the routine clinical need for vein of Marshall ethanol infusion remains an ongoing debate among electrophysiologists.

title: Procedural Success, Predictors of Failure, and Clinical Outcomes of Conduction System Pacing in Korea: The Korean Conduction System Pacing (K-CSP) Registry.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Conduction system pacing (CSP), particularly left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP), is a promising physiologic pacing strategy, but large-scale Asian data are lacking.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility, predictors of failure, and clinical outcomes of CSP in a nationwide Korean multicenter registry.
METHODS: This observational registry included 2,215 consecutive patients undergoing attempted CSP at 35 Korean centers between January 2021 and June 2025. Capture types were classified using EHRA criteria.
RESULTS: Stylet-driven leads were used in 87.0%. CSP succeeded in 87.4% (1,932/2,211). Among 1,922 LBBAP patients, left bundle branch pacing (LBBP) was achieved in 35.1%, left fascicular pacing (LFP) in 31.3%, and left ventricular septal pacing (LVSP) in 17.2%. Independent predictors of CSP failure included prior open-heart surgery involving septal manipulation, right-sided approach, and male sex. Pacing parameters were stable over 17.0±10.8 months. CSP failure was associated with worse composite outcomes on unadjusted analysis, but these associations were attenuated and no longer significant after adjustment. Among LBBAP patients, LVSP was associated with a higher adjusted risk of heart-failure hospitalization (adjusted HR 3.04, 95% CI 1.05-8.73, p=0.039) than LBBP+LFP; however, this association was based on few events with wide confidence intervals and was not significant on unadjusted analysis.
CONCLUSION: In this large-scale Asian CSP registry, LBBAP was feasible and safe, performed predominantly with stylet-driven leads. Direct conduction system capture (LBBP+LFP) was associated with a lower adjusted risk of heart-failure hospitalization than LVSP, although this was based on few events; these findings are hypothesis-generating and warrant confirmation in randomized trials.

score.why_it_matters: Provides large-scale real-world data on conduction system pacing in an Asian population, emphasizing the high feasibility of stylet-driven leads and predictors of procedural failure.
score.bottom_line: Left bundle branch area pacing had an 87.4% procedural success rate, with prior septal surgery, male sex, and right-sided access predicting failure. Achieving true conduction capture (LBBP/LFP) showed a potential reduction in heart failure hospitalizations compared to deep septal capture alone, though this requires randomized confirmation.

title: Author's reply to Targeting the Vein of Marshall in the Modern Era: Do We Still Need Ethanol?

score.why_it_matters: Provides author commentary on the ongoing debate regarding the utility of vein of Marshall ethanol infusion alongside contemporary catheter ablation strategies.
score.bottom_line: This is an author reply offering perspective on vein of Marshall ethanol ablation without presenting new primary trial data.

title: Leadless Atrial Pacing Targeting Bachmann Bundle for Atrial Resynchronization: A Single Center Registry.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Interatrial conduction delay (IACD) resulting from fibrosis or functional block in Bachmann bundle (BB) occurs often in patients with sinus node dysfunction (SND) and increases the risk of atrial fibrillation (AF). Pacing the BB in patients with SND may reduce AF burden. Little is known of the feasibility and effectiveness of BB leadless atrial pacemaker (BBLAP) implantation.
OBJECTIVE: To determine if BBLAP is safe, feasible and improves IACD.
METHODS: This registry prospectively enrolled 21 consecutive adults with baseline P wave duration (PWD) >120ms undergoing BBLAP for SND. Fluoroscopy, intracardiac echocardiography and left atrial conduction time (LACT) measurements from a decapolar coronary sinus (CS) catheter were used to facilitate implantation. BBLAP implant success was defined as improved PWD, P wave morphology, and LACT. Baseline and BBLAP LACT and PWD, axis, and morphology were compared.
RESULTS: Of the 21 patients enrolled, 17 had successful BBLAP (81%). Among those with successful BBLAP, baseline PWD was 150 (±21) ms, BBLAP PWD was 113 (±23) ms, a reduction of 37 (±13) ms, p < 0.001. BBLAP P wave axis was inferiorly directed in all cases. 8/8 patients with a negative terminal P wave in the inferior leads at baseline had correction with BBLAP. LACT decreased from 113 (±35) ms to 78 (±33) ms, mean difference 35 (±15) ms, p <0.001, with BBLAP. 13/17 patients demonstrated a shift in CS activation from proximal-distal activation to mid- or distal-proximal activation during BBLAP. In all cases there were no complications.
CONCLUSION: The BBLAP implant technique presented in this registry is feasible and reduced IACD. Further study on the effect of BBLAP on AF burden is needed.

score.why_it_matters: Demonstrates initial procedural feasibility of targeting Bachmann's bundle with a leadless atrial pacemaker to correct interatrial conduction delay.
score.bottom_line: In a 21-patient pilot registry, leadless Bachmann bundle pacing achieved an 81% success rate and significantly shortened P-wave duration and left atrial conduction time, though trials evaluating clinical endpoints like atrial fibrillation prevention are needed.

title: Distal-to-Proximal Conduction System Ablation as a Bailout Strategy in Refractory Multi-Exit Purkinje-Related Premature Ventricular Contractions and Ventricular Fibrillation.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ablation of premature ventricular contractions (PVCs) originating from the Purkinje network-particularly those with multiple exit sites and morphologies-poses a significant clinical challenge. In refractory cases where conventional ablation fails, proximal conduction system ablation may represent a viable alternative strategy.
OBJECTIVE: to evaluate the safety and efficacy of proximal conduction system ablation in patients with refractory multi-exit Purkinje PVCs with diverse morphologies.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort included consecutive patients with drug-refractory, symptomatic Purkinje PVCs who underwent proximal conduction system ablation. Multiple exit sites and morphologies were observed during mapping and ablation, indicating complex activation within the Purkinje network.
RESULTS: Among the 22 patients included, 14 (63.6%) had PVC-triggered ventricular fibrillation. Acute elimination of the PVC by distal-to-proximal conduction system ablation achieved in 21 patients (95.5%), while one procedure (4.5%) was discontinued at the patient's request due to the anticipated risk of conduction system injury. The initial site of earliest activation arose from the posterior fascicle in 63.6% (n=14), the septal fascicle in 22.7% (n=5) and the anterior fascicle in 13.6% (n=3). During ablation, all patients demonstrated a shift in the site of earliest activation. Conduction disturbances occurred in 5 patients (22.7%). During a median follow-up of 32.3 months (IQR 17.5-54.5), one patient (4.5%) experienced PVC recurrence requiring repeat ablation; however, no patient experienced recurrent ventricular fibrillation.
CONCLUSION: Distal-to-proximal conduction system ablation can be an effective bailout strategy for patients with refractory multi-exit fascicular/Purkinje-related PVCs and recurrent VF. Larger prospective studies are needed to confirm its long-term safety and efficacy.

score.why_it_matters: Provides a practical procedural bailout approach for highly refractory, multi-exit Purkinje-related PVCs triggering recurrent ventricular fibrillation.
score.bottom_line: A sequential distal-to-proximal ablation approach along the conduction system achieved acute PVC suppression in 95.5% of refractory cases and prevented VF recurrence, though at the expense of a 22.7% rate of conduction block.

title: Post-discharge care after adult cardiac surgery: a national survey of UK National Health Service centres.

score.why_it_matters: Understanding regional variations in post-discharge care pathways following cardiac surgery highlights gaps in continuity of care and transitional support.
score.bottom_line: This national survey benchmarks current UK NHS post-discharge follow-up practices after adult cardiac surgery, identifying substantial heterogeneity across centres.

title: Pulmonary Vein Isolation With Contact-Force-Sensing Large-Tip Focal Pulsed Field Ablation Catheter With 3D Mapping for Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation: Omny-IRE 12-month Results.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Omny-IRE (NCT05971693) evaluated safety and effectiveness of a large-tip focal, multielectrode, contact-force-sensing, pulsed field ablation, basket catheter with electroanatomic mapping integration.
OBJECTIVE: Report 12-month (M) study outcomes.
METHODS: Pulmonary vein isolation was performed using the OMNYPULSE platform. Patients underwent follow-up through 12M postablation visit with electrocardiography (preprocedure, predischarge, and at 1, 3, 6, and 12M), 24-hour Holter monitoring (3, 6, and 12M), and remote rhythm monitoring (weekly: 1-5M; monthly: 6-12M; and symptom-triggered recordings). The secondary effectiveness endpoint was 12M freedom from documented symptomatic/asymptomatic atrial arrhythmia (≥30 s) and acute procedural failure. Device/procedure-related serious adverse events (SAEs), quality-of-life assessed by Atrial Fibrillation Effect on Quality-of-Life (AFEQT) scores, and healthcare-utilization (cardiovascular-hospitalizations and antiarrhythmic drug [AAD] use) were also evaluated.
RESULTS: Among 188 enrolled patients, 136 comprised the main-phase-cohort for safety and effectiveness evaluations. In this cohort, 12M freedom from symptomatic/asymptomatic atrial arrhythmia was 82.5% (90.1% using standard-of-care monitoring only). Clinical success, defined as freedom from documented symptomatic arrhythmia and acute procedural failure, was 89.9%, while single procedural success was 89.2%. Device/procedure-related SAEs occurred in 2.9% of main-phase patients. Mean overall AFEQT score improved by 25.5 points from baseline to 12M. Cardiovascular-hospitalizations decreased by 40.9% versus the 12M preprocedure period, and Class I/III AAD use decreased by 49.3% 6-12M postablation versus baseline.
CONCLUSIONS: Omny-IRE results demonstrated the effectiveness, safety, and healthcare benefits of PFA with the OMNYPULSE platform.

score.why_it_matters: Provides 12-month clinical efficacy and safety data for a novel contact-force-sensing focal pulsed field ablation catheter integrated with 3D electroanatomic mapping for paroxysmal atrial fibrillation.
score.bottom_line: In the Omny-IRE study, pulmonary vein isolation using the OMNYPULSE platform achieved an 82.5% 12-month freedom from atrial arrhythmia with a low rate of serious adverse events (2.9%).

title: CATHETER ABLATION VERSUS SHAM FOR SYMPTOMATIC ATRIAL FIBRILLATION: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND BAYESIAN META-ANALYSIS OF RANDOMIZED TRIALS.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Catheter ablation reduces atrial fibrillation (AF) recurrence and improves symptoms and quality of life (QoL), but sham-controlled trials have reported discordant results.
OBJECTIVE: To synthesise sham-controlled trials of AF ablation and identify why QoL results differ.
METHODS: We searched databases and registries for randomized trials of catheter ablation versus sham in symptomatic AF. The primary outcome was the between-group difference in Atrial Fibrillation Effect on Quality-of-Life (AFEQT) score, pooled using a Bayesian random-effects model. Certainty was rated with the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation.
RESULTS: Four trials (468 patients) were eligible; three (448 patients) were pooled. Ablation improved AFEQT relative to sham by 13.5 points (95% credible interval [CrI] 1.6 to 26.9), with a posterior probability of benefit 0.98, of exceeding the 5-point minimal clinically important difference 0.94, and by 12.9 points (-0.4 to 27.1; probability 0.97 and 0.91) with PVI-SHAM-AF's primary estimator. Heterogeneity (τ 8.2 points, I2 85.3%) was largely attributed to PVI-SHAM-AF, which differed from the other trials in symptom severity, rhythm monitoring and assessment of blinding; without it, the difference was 18.9 points (6.7 to 31.4). Ablation reduced AF recurrence in every trial (pooled risk ratio 0.49, CrI 0.17-0.89). Certainty was moderate for AF burden and recurrence and low for QoL.
CONCLUSION: Compared with sham embedded in active rhythm control, catheter ablation reduces AF recurrence and burden and has a high probability of clinically important QoL benefit, although its magnitude remains uncertain. Trials differ in population, monitoring, and estimator, not direction of effect.

score.why_it_matters: By pooling sham-controlled trials, this meta-analysis confirms that catheter ablation provides true symptomatic and quality-of-life improvements that significantly exceed the placebo effect in atrial fibrillation.
score.bottom_line: Catheter ablation demonstrates a 94% probability of achieving a clinically meaningful quality-of-life benefit over sham procedures alongside a 51% reduction in AF recurrence. Apparent discrepancies among recent sham trials stem from variations in baseline symptom severity and monitoring rather than a lack of true treatment effect.

title: Non-Invasive Stimulation of the Median Nerve: Neuromodulation to Reduce Atrial Arrhythmias in Paroxysmal Atrial Fibrillation (The Randomized BEAT-AF Pilot Study).
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Non-invasive low-level electrical stimulation of the median nerve favorably affects atrial electrophysiology and reduces inflammation.
OBJECTIVE: To determine whether a novel wearable home-care neuromodulation device that performs median nerve stimulation (MNS) reduces atrial arrhythmias (AA) and related symptoms.
METHODS: BEAT-AF was a randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled, 12-week pilot study. Patients with a paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (AF) burden of 0.5-25% on ambulatory 14-day ECG (aECG) monitoring were randomized 1:1 to either MNS or Sham, using a wristband-like neuromodulation and ECG monitoring device.
RESULTS: Among 31 patients (n=15 MNS / n=16 Sham; age 67.3±9.7; 23 M / 8 F; CHA2DS2-VASc 2.6±1.7; median AF burden 4.9% [IQR 5.2%]),immediate pre-/post-treatment ECG recordings demonstrated a 35% reduction in premature atrial contraction (PAC) burden with MNS versus a 7% increase with Sham (p=0.039).Comparing baseline to 12-week 14-day ECGs, PAC burden was reduced by 26.5% (p=0.046) vs a numerical change of +3.94% (p=0.94; Sham, between group p=0.46), and the adjusted median AF burden numerically was reduced by 63% (MNS) vs 4.1% (Sham; p=0.42). By EHRA classification, symptomatology improved with MNS (0.45 vs 0.02 reduction in score; p=0.017), with a 26.3% shift from EHRA Class III to I with MNS) (vs Sham; p=0.048).
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with paroxysmal AF, non-invasive median nerve stimulation reduced PAC burden and improved symptomatology; there was a numerical but non-significant reduction in AF burden. This pilot study sets the stage for future pivotal trials of MNS in AF patients.

score.why_it_matters: This small pilot RCT explores non-invasive median nerve neuromodulation as a novel bioelectronic approach to suppress atrial ectopy and symptoms in paroxysmal AF.
score.bottom_line: In this 31-patient sham-controlled pilot trial, transcutaneous median nerve stimulation reduced PAC burden and improved EHRA symptom scores, though the reduction in overall AF burden did not reach statistical significance. Larger pivotal trials are required before clinical adoption.

title: Undiagnosed Arrhythmogenic Cardiomyopathy Hidden in Explanted Hearts: Insights from a Single Tertiary Center.

score.why_it_matters: Highlights diagnostic blind spots and underrecognition of arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy presenting as advanced or non-specific heart failure prior to transplantation.
score.bottom_line: Routine histopathological evaluation of explanted hearts can unmask previously unrecognized arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy, which is vital for initiating cascade genetic and clinical screening in surviving family members.

title: Mitral Valve Prolapse and Ventricular Arrhythmia Risk in TTN-Mediated Cardiomyopathy: A Single Center Experience.

score.why_it_matters: It explores the intersection of titin-truncating variants, mitral valve prolapse, and arrhythmogenic risk, highlighting a potentially high-risk phenotypic subgroup.
score.bottom_line: Concomitant mitral valve prolapse in patients with TTN-mediated cardiomyopathy may serve as an additional marker for increased ventricular arrhythmia risk, though larger multi-center validation is needed.

title: Interventricular septal LGE predicts response trajectories and clinical prognosis in heart failure patients undergoing left bundle branch area pacing.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) is an alternative strategy for heart failure (HF) patients with left bundle branch block (LBBB). Interventricular septal (IVS) fibrosis is linked to LBBAP efficacy.
OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between IVS late gadolinium enhancement percentage (IVS LGE%) and LBBAP response in non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (NICM) patients with LBBB.
METHODS: This was a two-center prospective observational study. Patients with NICM and complete LBBB were consecutively enrolled and received LBBAP from January 2021 to December 2024. Patients were divided into early, delayed, and non-response groups based on absolute left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) improvement ≥5% at 6 and 12 months.
RESULTS: A total of 113 patients were included, with 86 (76.1%) early responders, 13 (11.5%) delayed responders, and 14 (12.4%) non-responders. IVS LGE% linearly increased the risk of non-early response, with each 1% increase conferring a 14% higher risk of adverse response progression (early to delayed or non-response) (adjusted OR=1.14, 95%CI 1.05-1.23; P=0.002). 75.3% of IVS fibrosis-related 6-month impairment was mediated by failed LBB captured (direct effect P=0.204), while the direct inhibitory effect of IVS fibrosis emerged at 12 months (mediation proportion 60.8%, β=-0.33, P=0.005). Optimal IVS LGE% cut-off values were 7.62% for early response and 12.33% for delayed response, with 12-month response rates of 95.06%, 93.75% and 43.75% across low, intermediate and high IVS LGE% groups, respectively.
CONCLUSION: IVS fibrosis independently predicts LBBAP response and prognosis in NICM patients with complete LBBB, and modulates LBBAP efficacy through a time-dependent biphasic mechanism.

score.why_it_matters: Identifies septal fibrosis on cardiac MRI as a key predictor of lead capture failure and attenuated reverse remodeling following left bundle branch area pacing.
score.bottom_line: In non-ischemic cardiomyopathy patients undergoing LBBAP for LBBB, higher interventricular septal LGE is associated with delayed or absent LVEF recovery, with extensive fibrosis (>12%) resulting in poor 12-month response rates.

title: Transvenous Lead Extraction Without Dedicated Surgical Back up in Low-Risk Patients.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transvenous lead extraction (TLE) is associated with major complications that could require immediate surgical rescue. These procedures are performed in an EP lab or hybrid OR with the presence of a surgical team on standby. We have designed an institutional protocol that permits performance of TLE in low-risk situations, in an EP lab without dedicated surgical back-up.
OBJECTIVES: To investigate outcomes of TLE in low-risk patients METHODS: We retrospectively identified patients who underwent low-risk TLE at Emory Healthcare between 2010-23. Low-risk TLE were defined as an extraction of a pacing or ICD lead with a dwell time >= 1 and <= 5 years or a lead < 1 year that required extraction tools.
RESULTS: Among 482 patients who met the criteria, the average lead age was 2.8 ± 1.2 years. The mean number of targeted leads per patient was 1.6±0.7. Extraction tools were required in 33.1% of cases. Major complications occurred in 0.83% of patients (n=4): 2 pericardial effusions requiring pericardiocentesis, 1 pneumothorax and 1 death from cardiogenic shock in an end stage heart failure patient. The patients with pericardial effusions and pneumothorax were part of a procedure that required lead revisions and the insertion of 1 or more new leads. No patients required surgical rescue.
CONCLUSION: This study suggests that, in selected "low-risk" patients, TLE can be performed safely in an experienced EP lab at centers with on-site cardiac surgery but without a dedicated surgical standby team, potentially reducing resource utilization in resource-limited healthcare environments.

score.why_it_matters: Demonstrates that transvenous lead extraction in carefully selected low-risk patients (lead dwell time 1–5 years) may be performed safely without active surgical standby, provided on-site surgical capabilities exist.
score.bottom_line: In a retrospective cohort of 482 low-risk lead extractions, major complications occurred in 0.83% and zero patients required surgical rescue. While hypothesis-generating for optimizing EP lab resource utilization, standard safety precautions and prompt access to emergency cardiac surgery remain essential.

title: Bench Evaluation of Pulsed Field Ablation Interference With Left Atrial Appendage Closure Devices.

score.why_it_matters: Evaluates potential electrical and structural interactions between pulsed field ablation and preexisting or concomitant left atrial appendage closure devices in a bench model.
score.bottom_line: This preclinical bench study provides initial technical safety insights regarding pulsed field ablation delivery near implanted left atrial appendage closure devices, though clinical validation is required.

title: Effect of telemedicine-based integrated management of atrial fibrillation in village clinics on recurrent nonfatal cardiovascular events: a secondary analysis of the MIRACLE-AF trial.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is an increasing public health challenge, particularly among rural older adults, where awareness and treatment remain inadequate. While the MIRACLE-AF trial demonstrated that telemedicine-based, village doctor-led integrated care reduced cardiovascular mortality or first major cardiovascular events, its impact on recurrent nonfatal cardiovascular events remains unknown.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the effect of the MIRACLE-AF care model on recurrent nonfatal cardiovascular events.
METHODS: We conducted a secondary analysis of the MIRACLE-AF trial (NCT04622514), a cluster-randomized controlled trial enrolling 1,039 rural patients aged ≥65 years with confirmed AF across 30 village clinics over 36 months. Village clinics were randomized 1:1 to village doctor-led telemedicine integrated care or enhanced usual care. The primary outcome was recurrent nonfatal events over 36 months, including strokes, hospitalizations for worsening heart failure or acute coronary syndrome, and emergency visits for AF, analyzed using a conditional frailty model.
RESULTS: Among 1039 patients (mean age 75.8 ± 5.7 years; 44.3% female), the intervention experienced fewer cardiovascular events than the control (118 events in 82 patients [15.65%] vs. 173 events in 122 patients [23.69%]). The observed recurrent event rates were 6.75 and 9.11 per 100 patient-years, respectively. The estimated hazard ratio was 0.76 (95% CI, 0.583-1.004; p = 0.053), indicating that the difference did not reach statistical significance.
CONCLUSION: Although the overall difference did not reach statistical significance, directional trends consistently favored telemedicine-based integrated care, suggesting a potential reduction in recurrent cardiovascular event burden. Larger studies with longer follow-up are needed to confirm these findings.

score.why_it_matters: Provides insights into whether community-level telemedicine interventions can reduce cumulative recurrent cardiovascular admissions and stroke in underserved rural populations with atrial fibrillation.
score.bottom_line: In this secondary analysis of the MIRACLE-AF cluster-randomized trial, village doctor-led telemedicine care showed a favorable numerical trend but did not statistically significantly reduce recurrent nonfatal cardiovascular events over 36 months (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.58–1.00; p = 0.053).

title: Association of Left Atrial Intramyocardial Fat Infiltration With Atrial Arrhythmia Recurrence After Pulsed-Field Ablation for Persistent Atrial Fibrillation.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Computed tomography (CT)-derived left atrial intramyocardial fat infiltration (inFAT) is an emerging imaging phenotype of the atrial substrate in atrial fibrillation (AF).
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate inFAT and peri-left atrial epicardial adipose tissue (LA-EAT) using artificial intelligence-based CT analysis software (ADAS 3D) and to assess their association with atrial arrhythmia recurrence after persistent AF ablation.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 59 patients who underwent pulsed-field ablation for persistent AF. inFAT and LA-EAT were quantified using a semi-automated algorithm. Cox regression analysis was performed to evaluate the association of inFAT and LA-EAT with recurrence. Kaplan-Meier analysis was performed after stratification according to the tertile of each parameter.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up period of 11.2 [6.4-11.9] months, atrial arrhythmia recurrence occurred in 21 (36%) patients. The inFAT volume was significantly greater in patients with recurrence than those without (1.25 [0.78-1.53] vs. 0.72 [0.45-1.09] cm3, p=0.021). In contrast, LA-EAT volume was comparable between the groups (21.8 [13.7-30.4] vs. 17.5 [14.1-26.8] cm3, p=0.419). In Cox regression analysis, higher inFAT was significantly associated with recurrence, whereas LA-EAT was not significantly associated (inFAT: hazard ratio [HR], 1.93; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.13-3.27; p=0.015; LA-EAT: HR, 1.02; 95% CI, 0.99-1.06; p=0.227). The significant association between inFAT and recurrence remained consistent after adjustment for body mass index.
CONCLUSIONS: Greater inFAT volume was associated with atrial arrhythmia recurrence after pulsed-field ablation for persistent AF, suggesting that inFAT may represent a candidate imaging marker of recurrence risk.

score.why_it_matters: Identifies CT-derived left atrial intramyocardial fat infiltration as a potential novel imaging biomarker for arrhythmia recurrence following pulsed-field ablation in persistent atrial fibrillation.
score.bottom_line: In this small retrospective study of 59 patients, increased left atrial intramyocardial fat volume was associated with higher recurrence rates after pulsed-field ablation for persistent AF. These preliminary findings warrant validation in larger, prospective cohorts before impacting clinical workflow.

title: Sex-based differences in bi-atrial voltage in atrial fibrillation: a multimodal and digital twin approach to distinguish physiological variation from pathological remodelling.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sex-based differences in atrial voltage have been reported in atrial fibrillation (AF), but it is unclear whether these differences reflect pathological remodelling or physiological variation.
OBJECTIVE: To assess sex-based differences in voltage, contextualised by complementary measures of substrate remodelling and AF mechanisms.
METHODS: A multicentre, prospective study was conducted in patients scheduled for AF ablation. Bi-atrial voltage mapping was combined with electrophysiological assessment, structural and functional assessment using cardiac MRI, and mechanistic interrogation using patient-specific digital twins. Propensity score matching was used to account for baseline differences between sexes. Exploratory receiver operating characteristic analysis was conducted to estimate sex-specific mean left atrial voltage cutoffs based on 12-month arrhythmia recurrence status.
RESULTS: Seventy patients (62±12 years; 31% female) were included. Women demonstrated lower mean bipolar voltages than men, with this difference persisting after 1:1 propensity score matching (n=44) in both left (1.66±0.71mV versus 2.12±0.55mV, p=0.028) and right atria (1.79±0.49mV versus 2.20±0.59mV, p=0.025). Propensity score-matched analyses revealed no significant differences in other structural, functional, or electrophysiological parameters, with digital twin analyses demonstrating no significant differences in AF termination, phase singularity count, wave dynamics, or response to virtual ablation. Women had lower mean left atrial voltage cutoffs calibrated to 12-month arrhythmia recurrence status than men (1.74mV versus 2.26mV).
CONCLUSIONS: Women with AF exhibit lower bi-atrial voltages despite comparable substrate characteristics and AF mechanisms, suggesting that observed voltage differences may reflect physiological variation rather than pathological remodelling. Sex-specific voltage thresholds may improve the accuracy of substrate assessment and facilitate personalised treatment.

score.why_it_matters: Demonstrates that baseline bi-atrial voltages are physiologically lower in women compared to men despite identical AF substrate dynamics, suggesting standard low-voltage thresholds may lead to over-diagnosis of atrial scar in female patients.
score.bottom_line: Lower atrial voltages in women appear to reflect physiological differences rather than advanced pathological remodelling, pointing toward a need for sex-adjusted voltage thresholds during AF substrate mapping.

title: Atrial Fibrillation Pattern and Outcomes After Contemporary Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Atrial fibrillation (AF) pattern predicts thromboembolic risk during anticoagulation, but its prognostic importance after left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is uncertain.
OBJECTIVES: To determine whether AF pattern independently predicts residual clinical risk after contemporary LAAO and whether peri-device leak (PDL) or device-related thrombus (DRT) identify a persistently high-risk subgroup.
METHODS: We studied 3,459 patients with documented AF pattern undergoing LAAO in a contemporary multicenter registry. AF was classified as paroxysmal, persistent or long-standing persistent, or permanent. The primary endpoint was a 2-year hierarchical composite of death, stroke or systemic embolism (stroke/SE), and major bleeding analyzed by win ratio. Inverse probability weighting and propensity score methods adjusted for baseline differences. Follow-up imaging assessed PDL and DRT.
RESULTS: After inverse probability weighting, persistent and permanent AF were associated with progressively worse hierarchical outcomes compared with paroxysmal AF (win ratios 1.39 and 1.59, respectively). Non-paroxysmal AF was associated with higher stroke risk (HR 1.64; 95% CI 1.07-2.50), without increased mortality or major bleeding. PDL and DRT were more frequent in non-paroxysmal AF. In the PDL/DRT subgroup, non-paroxysmal AF was associated with higher first stroke/SE risk (HR 1.83; 95% CI 1.00-3.34), concentrated 180-540 days after LAAO.
CONCLUSIONS: AF pattern independently stratified residual clinical risk after LAAO, with progressively worse severity-weighted outcomes from paroxysmal to persistent and permanent AF. Excess risk was driven primarily by thromboembolism. In the PDL/DRT subgroup, the association was concentrated 180-540 days after LAAO, suggesting these patients may benefit from prolonged thromboembolic surveillance.

score.why_it_matters: Demonstrates that baseline AF pattern independently predicts residual stroke risk and device-related complications after left atrial appendage occlusion, challenging the notion that mechanical closure eliminates AF-pattern-dependent thromboembolic risk.
score.bottom_line: Patients with persistent or permanent AF experience higher rates of stroke, peri-device leak, and device-related thrombus following LAAO compared to those with paroxysmal AF. Closer and extended surveillance, particularly between 6 and 18 months post-procedure, may be warranted in non-paroxysmal cohorts.

title: Left Atrial Reservoir Strain To Identify Advanced Atrial Cardiomyopathy in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left atrial reservoir strain (LASr) is a novel marker of left atrial (LA) function. We hypothesized that LASr can be used to identify atrial cardiomyopathy in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF).
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the association between LASr and invasive and non-invasive markers of atrial cardiomyopathy in AF patients.
METHODS: We prospectively recruited patients with symptomatic paroxysmal or persistent AF and preserved left ventricular (LV) ejection fraction scheduled for catheter ablation. Resting transthoracic echocardiography was performed focusing on the left atrium (LA). Participants were dichotomised into two groups: reduced LASr (<20%) and preserved LASr (≥20%). Markers of LA cardiomyopathy were compared between these two groups; invasive markers included mean LA pressure, mean LA voltage and LA compliance whilst non-invasive markers included LA volumes and NT-pro BNP.
RESULTS: A total of 91 patients were enrolled. Patients with reduced LASr (n=31) were older (69.4±8.9 vs 59.6±11.3 years, p<0.001), and more commonly female (45.2 vs 18.3%, p=0.007). Reduced LASr correlated with lower LA compliance (0.28±0.16 vs 0.42±0.25mm/mmHg, p<0.001), higher LA pressure (14.8±3.81 vs 13.1±4.46mmHg, p=0.031), and lower LA voltage (1.65±1.35 vs 3.12±1.57mV, p<0.01). On non-invasive assessment, reduced LASr was also associated with higher NT-proBNP levels (479 [200-1073] vs 121 [58-256] pg/ml p<0.001) and larger LA volumes (38.5±11.5 vs 32.6±7.7 mL/m2, p<0.001).
CONCLUSION: In patients with symptomatic AF, reduced LASr is associated with a more advanced atrial cardiomyopathy involving hemodynamic, mechanical and electrical atrial dyfsfunction. LASr may therefore provide a useful non-invasive marker of atrial cardiomyopathy in AF.

score.why_it_matters: Demonstrates that non-invasive left atrial reservoir strain correlates with invasive hemodynamic and electroanatomic markers of atrial cardiomyopathy in patients undergoing AF ablation.
score.bottom_line: Reduced left atrial reservoir strain (<20%) is associated with lower atrial voltage, higher filling pressures, and reduced atrial compliance in symptomatic AF patients. While useful as a non-invasive surrogate for advanced substrate, its routine use to alter ablation strategy requires larger prospective outcome trials.

title: Pulmonary vein narrowing after voltage-guided adjunctive pulmonary vein sleeve pulsed field ablation.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) for pulmonary vein (PV) isolation (PVI) has been associated with a low risk of PV stenosis when performed using the standard ostial workflow. However, the risk of PV narrowing after adjunctive PV sleeve PFA remains insufficiently evaluated.
OBJECTIVE: To assess PV narrowing after voltage-guided adjunctive PV sleeve PFA.
METHODS: We retrospectively studied 147 patients who underwent an initial pentaspline PFA-based PVI for atrial fibrillation. In addition to standard ostial PVI, voltage-guided PFA applications were delivered to target PV sleeve potentials identified on pre-ablation voltage mapping. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography was performed before and approximately six months after ablation. PV cross-sectional areas (PVAs) were measured at predefined levels, and the maximum PVA reduction rate was defined as ΔPVA. Significant PV narrowing was defined as ΔPVA ≥25%.
RESULTS: Post-ablation PVA was significantly smaller than pre-ablation PVA at all PV sites. The median ΔPVA was 5.4%, 6.4%, 4.6%, and 4.0% in the left superior, left inferior, right superior, and right inferior PVs, respectively, and differed significantly among the four PV sites (P = 0.012). No significant PV narrowing was observed in this cohort.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients undergoing an initial PFA-based PVI, no significant PV narrowing was observed approximately six months after voltage-guided adjunctive PV sleeve PFA using a pentaspline catheter. Further controlled studies with larger populations and longer follow-up are needed to better characterize the safety and clinical utility of this strategy.

score.why_it_matters: Demonstrates the mid-term safety profile of delivering pulsed field ablation deeper into pulmonary vein sleeves without causing clinically significant stenosis.
score.bottom_line: In this retrospective series of 147 patients, voltage-guided adjunctive PV sleeve pulsed field ablation resulted in minimal cross-sectional area reduction (median 4-6%) and zero cases of significant PV narrowing (≥25%) at 6 months on CT.

title: Zero-fluoroscopy approach to left atrial appendage closure using intracardiac echo guidance.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) with the Watchman™ device is typically performed with the use of transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) and fluoroscopy. LAAC guided by intracardiac echo (ICE) without the use of fluoroscopy has not been previously described.
OBJECTIVE: In this series, we describe the safety and feasibility of Watchman™ implantation using only ICE imaging and without the use of fluoroscopy.
METHODS: 214 patients undergoing LAAC with the Watchman FLX™ or Watchman FLX™ Pro device and using a planned fluoroscopy-free approach were studied. ICE was used for echocardiographic imaging in all cases. TEE was not used in any cases. Fluoroscopy was used as a bail-out approach when it was felt to be clinically necessary by the operator. Peri-procedural, 45-day, and 1-year efficacy and safety outcomes were assessed.
RESULTS: In 203/214 patients (94.8%), LAAC was completed without the use of fluoroscopy. Bail-out fluoroscopy was required in 11/214 patients (5.1%). Successful device implantation was completed in 212/214 patients (99.1%). The rate of any peri-device leak at 45 days post-procedure was 11.6%. Procedural complications were limited to one pericardial effusion and one case of ventricular tachycardia.
CONCLUSION: LAAC with the Watchman™ device using ICE imaging and without the use of fluoroscopy appears to be safe and effective. The rates of procedural success, complications, and peri-device leaks on 45 day follow up were consistent with that seen in pivotal clinical trials. Further studies are needed to assess the broader applicability of this technique.

score.why_it_matters: Demonstrates the feasibility of completely eliminating radiation exposure during Watchman implantation using ICE guidance alone, potentially protecting operators and patients.
score.bottom_line: In this 214-patient cohort, a zero-fluoroscopy ICE-guided approach to LAAC was successful in ~95% of cases with low complication rates, though bailout fluoroscopy remained necessary in 5%.

title: Prognostic Impact of Ventricular Arrhythmia Timing in Acute Coronary Syndromes Treated with Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ventricular arrhythmias (VA) often complicate acute coronary syndromes (ACS). The prognostic impact of VA timing relative to percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains unclear.
OBJECTIVE: To assess the prognostic significance of VA based on their timing of occurrence in relation to PCI.
METHODS: Systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies reporting all-cause mortality with and without VA (sustained or hemodynamically unstable VT/VF) in ACS patients undergoing PCI. The endpoints analyzed were short-term (30 days/in-hospital) and long-term (1 year) mortality. A network meta-analysis comparing VA-before PCI, VA-during PCI, and VA-after PCI with the group not experiencing VA as a reference was conducted.
RESULTS: Twelve studies comprising 49,963 patients were included, of whom 3,475 (7.0%) experienced VA. VA was associated with increased short- (OR 5.04, 95%CI 3.78-6.72) and long-term mortality (OR 2.92, 95%CI 2.20-3.86). In patients alive at discharge/30 days, subsequent long-term mortality risk did not differ between those with and without VA (OR 0.97, 95%CI 0.62-1.52). The network meta-analysis showed that all VA timings are associated with a significantly higher risk compared with the group not experiencing VA. Sensitivity analysis found that VA-after is associated with higher short-term mortality than earlier VA (OR 3.37, 95%CI 1.46-7.82).
CONCLUSIONS: VA substantially increase the risk of death in patients with ACS undergoing PCI. Mortality risk emerges to be associated with the timing of VA occurrence, with VA-after PCI associated with the highest risk. These findings highlight the prognostic relevance of arrhythmic events across the entire peri-procedural window, underscoring the need for refined risk stratification.

score.why_it_matters: Clarifies that while any peri-PCI ventricular arrhythmia increases acute mortality, arrhythmias occurring post-PCI carry the highest short-term risk, whereas 30-day survivors have comparable long-term outcomes to non-arrhythmic patients.
score.bottom_line: In patients with ACS undergoing PCI, post-PCI ventricular arrhythmias confer a significantly higher risk of short-term death compared to pre- or intra-procedural events. However, once patients survive past 30 days or hospital discharge, long-term mortality risk normalizes.

title: Day-Night Patterns of Wearable-Derived Electrocardiographic Age and Left Atrial Remodeling in Atrial Fibrillation-Naïve Individuals.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Artificial intelligence-derived electrocardiographic (AI-ECG) age is conventionally treated as a static marker. Its diurnal dynamics and structural correlates in individuals without atrial fibrillation (AF) remain unknown.
OBJECTIVE: To characterize diurnal AI-ECG age patterns, their reproducibility, and associations with left atrial (LA) remodeling.
METHODS: We analyzed continuous wearable ECGs from two prospective registries (NCT05119725, NCT05355948). In 499 AF-naïve participants with ≥48-hour recordings, AI-ECG age was estimated every 10 minutes. Unsupervised clustering identified day-night trajectories, summarized by day-night difference (ΔAge) into Restorative (>0.6 years) or Disrupted (≤0.6 years) phenotypes. Reproducibility was evaluated across sequential periods. Age- and sex-adjusted associations of binary and continuous ΔAge with LA volume index (LAVI) were pooled in a cross-sectional echocardiographic substudy (n=122).
RESULTS: Three trajectories emerged in both registries. Restorative prevalence was 47.6%-50.2%. Agreement between two consecutive 48-hour periods was 75.8% (κ = 0.516; 95% CI, 0.395-0.631); 6- to 8-day intraclass correlation coefficients were 0.51-0.54. The Disrupted phenotype was associated with higher LAVI (pooled mean difference, 5.54 mL/m2; 95% CI, 1.11-9.98; P = .014) and greater odds of LA enlargement (LAVI ≥40 mL/m2; pooled odds ratio, 3.68; 95% CI, 1.45-9.29; P = .006). Per 1-SD higher ΔAge, LAVI was lower (β, -2.89 mL/m2; P = .007) and LA enlargement less likely (odds ratio, 0.53; P = .004).
CONCLUSION: Wearable-derived AI-ECG age exhibits a reproducible day-night pattern. A Disrupted phenotype is associated with adverse LA remodeling. Because reproducibility remains insufficient for individual-level classification, prospective outcome-based validation is warranted.

score.why_it_matters: Demonstrates that dynamic diurnal fluctuations in wearable AI-ECG age correlate with left atrial enlargement, though reproducibility remains suboptimal for current bedside application.
score.bottom_line: Loss of normal day-night reductions in AI-derived ECG age ('disrupted phenotype') is associated with adverse left atrial remodeling in AF-naïve individuals. However, moderate reproducibility limits its current clinical utility as an individual-level screening tool.

title: Ten-year Performance of the Multi-Layer Insulated Defibrillation Lead in the Medicare Population.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Long-term surveillance of implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) leads is essential because clinically important mechanical failures may emerge years after implantation.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate 10-year mechanical complication-free survival of the Optisure ICD lead (Abbott, Sylmar, CA) in a large real-world Medicare population.
METHODS: Manufacturer device-tracking records were linked to Medicare Fee-for-Service claims and device complaint data using the EP PASSION framework. Patients receiving an Optisure lead from February 2014 through December 2024 were included. Mechanical lead-related complications were defined by claims containing both a diagnosis of mechanical lead malfunction and a lead-related surgical intervention more than 30 days after implantation. Kaplan-Meier survival was estimated under a best-case scenario including confirmed Optisure-related events and a worst-case scenario also including potentially related events.
RESULTS: The cohort included 26,830 patients with 27,033 Optisure leads. Mean age was 73.8 ± 8.6 years, 28.4% were women, and 49.8% had cardiac resynchronization therapy ICDs. Overall, 379 complications were classified as confirmed lead-related and 606 as confirmed or potentially lead-related. At 10 years, complication-free lead survival was 97.2% (95% confidence interval [CI], 96.7%-97.7%) in the best-case scenario and 95.6% (95% CI, 94.9%-96.2%) in the worst-case scenario. Survival did not differ significantly by age, lead length, coil configuration, or device type.
CONCLUSION: The Optisure ICD lead demonstrated favorable mechanical performance through 10 years in routine clinical practice. These findings support both the long-term durability of Optisure and the use of integrated real-world data for post-market device surveillance.

score.why_it_matters: Provides reassuring long-term real-world surveillance data demonstrating high mechanical durability and low failure rates for the Optisure ICD lead out to 10 years.
score.bottom_line: In a real-world Medicare cohort of over 26,000 patients, 10-year mechanical complication-free survival of the Optisure ICD lead was excellent at 95.6% to 97.2%. These findings confirm sustained reliability without late mechanical failure signals.

title: Epicardial Closure for Peridevice Leaks from Endocardial Left Atrial Appendage Closure - Early LARIAT-4-PDL Registry Results.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Closure of clinically significant peri-device leaks (PDLs) after left atrial appendage (LAA) occlusion remains crucial to prevent thromboembolism. A variety of techniques exist to close PDLs, each with its own advantages and disadvantages. The LARIAT (Atricure, Mason, OH) suture device may provide an alternative for closing PDLs.
OBJECTIVE: We report the initial feasibility of LARIAT for endocardial LAA closure PDLs.
METHODS: In a multicenter, retrospective study, we reviewed consecutive patients who underwent LARIAT for closure of device-related LAA leaks. All patients had PDLs ≥3 mm after either a Watchman FLX Pro (Boston Scientific, Marlborough, MA) or an Amplatzer Amulet (Abbott, Chicago, IL) endocardial LAA occluder, as seen on postoperative imaging. Acute PDL closure - pericardial access with device deployment and elimination of the PDL on intraprocedural imaging - was evaluated with either transesophageal or intracardiac echocardiogram, along with 45-day safety.
RESULTS: We report 10 cases in patients aged 67.2±10.7years, 30.0% female, and with a body mass index 32.4±6.4 kg/m2. Baseline comorbidities included a CHADSVASC of 4.4±0.7 and HASBLED of 3.7±0.7. Initially, patients underwent Watchman (80.0%) or Amulet (20.0%) with an average PDL of 5.4±0.8 mm. Few cases had attempted PDL closure with radiofrequency ablation (10.0%), coiling (20.0%), or a previous device (10.0%). After procedural and fluoroscopy times of 48.7±10.8 min and 7.0±3.7 min, respectively, LARIAT PDL closure was successful in all cases, and no difference when stratified by initial endocardial LAA closure type.
CONCLUSION: These initial results suggest that a LARIAT may be an alternative strategy in patients with clinically significant PDLs after endocardial LAA closure. Future studies are needed to corroborate our initial findings and long-term closure results.

score.why_it_matters: Provides preliminary proof-of-concept for using an epicardial suture-ligation system as an alternative bail-out strategy to manage large peridevice leaks after endocardial left atrial appendage occlusion.
score.bottom_line: In this early 10-patient registry, LARIAT epicardial closure demonstrated acute procedural feasibility for closing persistent, large (≥3 mm) peridevice leaks after Watchman or Amulet implantation. Larger prospective series are needed before this can be broadly adopted into clinical practice.

title: A Technique for Slack Formation During Proximal Left Bundle Branch Pacing With a Lumenless Defibrillation Lead.

score.why_it_matters: Proper lead slack is crucial during conduction system pacing with defibrillator leads to prevent mechanical failure, dislodgement, or late perforation.
score.bottom_line: This technical report describes a procedural maneuver to optimize slack formation when deploying a lumenless defibrillation lead targeting the proximal left bundle branch.

title: Short-term safety, feasibility, and performance of a novel soft robotic biventricular mechanical circulatory support device avoiding blood contact - The MISSION reBEAT trial.
abstract:
AIMS: Mechanical Circulatory Support (MCS) remains limited in advanced heart failure due to blood-contact complications and the absence of biventricular support. We report the first prospective clinical trial of a novel soft-robotic, biventricular, pulsatile technology placed externally around the heart without blood contact, designed to deliver individualized cardiac assistance (reBEAT®, AdjuCor GmbH, Munich, Germany).
METHODS AND RESULTS: The system was temporarily applied in 10 end-stage heart failure patients immediately before elective LVAD implantation. Devices were custom-manufactured using preoperative CT scans to match individual cardiac anatomy. Safety, feasibility, and effects on haemodynamics were evaluated. Implantation was rapid (3±2 min), demonstrating procedural feasibility. We observed two procedure-related adverse events while no device- or procedure-related severe adverse events occurred. Absence of new ECG abnormalities, and no tissue injury confirmed safety. An iterative assessment on haemodynamics provided key insights into individualized cardio-circulatory support. While device presence reduced preload dependent haemodynamics in some patients, low average support pressures of 65-66 mmHg produced variable improvements towards baseline, predominantly on the pressure signal: mean arterial pressure (MAP; 67.5 ± 10.6 vs. 76.2 ± 11.7 mmHg, p<0.01), stroke work (SW; 347.8 ± 118.2 vs. 434.1 ± 131.0 mJ, p<0.01), and cardiac power output (CPO; 407.9 ± 108.2 vs. 503.7 ± 116.2 mW, p<0.01). Additionally, effects were observed on atrioventricular valve function and interventricular balance, which were not significant.
CONCLUSION: This soft-robotic biventricular MCS platform provides short term evidence of a safe and feasible approach to pulsatile biventricular support without blood contact. Significant increases in MAP, CPO, and SW towards baseline indicate functional effects. Continuous device-driven workflow improvement is mandatory and further data are required to refine individualized optimization strategies. This technology may offer a novel biventricular assist modality. Its reduced complexity may enable broader adaption for both temporary and durable support. Avoiding blood contact and enabling balanced biventricular assistance will be central drivers of its continued clinical development.

score.why_it_matters: This first-in-human study demonstrates the feasibility of an epicardial, soft-robotic biventricular assist device that avoids blood contact, offering a novel proof-of-concept to mitigate hemocompatibility-related adverse events.
score.bottom_line: In 10 patients evaluated acutely prior to LVAD placement, the epicardial reBEAT system was implanted rapidly and safely, providing modest hemodynamic improvements. While promising as an alternative to blood-contacting MCS, extensive development and longer-term clinical data are required before clinical adoption.

title: Sex differences in cardiovascular disease burden, risk factors, and disease spectrum in Europe: a global burden of disease 2023 analysis within the ESC Atlas framework.
abstract: Despite growing recognition of sex disparities in cardiovascular disease (CVD), contemporary, harmonized analyses of sex-specific burden in the European region that could inform targeted prevention strategies, remain limited. Sex-specific patterns in CVD burden and risk factor exposure across 55 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) member countries were examined using data from the 2023 Global Burden of Disease study. Risk factor exposure was quantified using age-sex-standardized summary exposure values for 10 established cardiovascular risk factors. Disease incidence and mortality for major CVD categories, including maternal hypertensive disorders, were estimated by calculating age-sex-standardized rates per 100 000 person-years using the 2013 European Standard Population. Analyses were performed by sex at country, regional, and ESC-wide levels and over time (1990-2023). In 2023, in the ESC region, the overall CVD burden was broadly similar in men and women, with women accounting for 55% (6.0 million) of cases and 50% of deaths (1.5 million). This apparent parity, however, concealed marked sex differences in disease composition, risk exposure, and geographic disparities. Compared with men, women had a lower proportion of CVD due to ischaemic heart disease (21% vs 38%) and a higher contribution from peripheral arterial disease (23% vs 19%). Major differences were also apparent in risk profiles, particularly for behavioural risk factors-with summary exposure values of tobacco and alcohol being 10%-20% points higher in men than women; contrasting with cardiometabolic factors, such as high body mass index and low physical activity, that were often 5%-15% points higher in women than men, and more modest differences in environmental and biological risks, including air pollution, fasting glucose, or cholesterol. Cardiovascular disease burden further varied widely across countries and disparities affected women more strongly than men, with an approximately three-fold difference between the lowest- and highest-incidence countries in women, compared with a two-fold difference in men, and even larger disparities in mortality and premature mortality (up to 25-fold in women). Maternal hypertensive disorders substantially shaped both the scale and composition of CVD burden in women, accounting for 25% of incident CVD in women and exhibiting substantial geographic variation, with up to 18-fold differences in incidence across countries. These findings challenge conventional approaches that treat CVD as a homogeneous condition. In particular, the substantial contribution of non-ischaemic conditions and maternal hypertensive disorders to the burden in women, alongside distinct patterns of risk exposure and wider geographic disparities, underscore the importance of adopting a life-course and sex- and gender-informed approach to cardiovascular prevention and policy.

score.why_it_matters: This comprehensive GBD 2023 analysis reveals that despite equal overall CVD mortality between sexes in Europe, women suffer significantly more non-ischemic CVD and maternal hypertensive disorders, with larger geographic health disparities.
score.bottom_line: Cardiovascular prevention in women must look beyond traditional obstructive CAD, aggressively addressing maternal hypertensive disorders—which drive 25% of female incident CVD—alongside obesity and physical inactivity.
